verses.1:1: Now King David was old, advanced in days, and they covered him with garments, yet he could not grow warm.
verses.1:2: So his servants said to him, "Let them search for a young virgin woman for my lord the king, and let her stand before the king and be a caretaker for him; let her lie in your embrace, so that my lord the king may grow warm."
verses.1:3: They searched for a beautiful young woman throughout all the territory of Israel, found Abishag the Shunammite, and brought her to the king.
verses.1:4: Now the young woman was exceedingly beautiful; she became a caretaker for the king and waited on him, but the king did not know her.
verses.1:5: Now Adonijah son of Haggith was exalting himself, saying, "I will reign." So he provided chariots and horsemen for himself, along with fifty men running ahead of him.
verses.1:6: And his father had never grieved him in all his days by asking, "Why have you acted like this?" He was also very handsome in appearance, and he was born after Absalom.
verses.1:7: He held discussions with Joab son of Zeruiah and with Abiathar the priest, and they sided with Adonijah and supported him.
verses.1:8: Yet Zadok the priest, Benaiah son of Jehoiada, Nathan the prophet, Shimei, Rei, and the mighty warriors who belonged to David were not with Adonijah.
verses.1:9: Then Adonijah sacrificed sheep, cattle, and fattened calves by the Stone of Zoheleth, which is next to En-rogel; he invited all his brothers, the sons of the king, along with all the men of Judah, the servants of the king.
verses.1:10: But Nathan the prophet, Benaiah, the mighty warriors, and his brother Solomon he did not invite.
verses.1:11: Then Nathan spoke to Bathsheba, Solomon's mother, saying, "Have you not heard that Adonijah son of Haggith has become king, while our lord David does not know?
verses.1:12: Now come, please let me offer you counsel, and rescue your life and the life of your son Solomon.
verses.1:13: Go and come in to King David, and say to him, 'Did you not yourself, my lord the king, swear to your female servant, saying, "Surely your son Solomon will reign after me, and he himself will sit on my throne"? Why then has Adonijah become king?'
verses.1:14: Look, while you are still speaking there with the king, I myself will enter after you and corroborate your words."
verses.1:15: So Bathsheba went in to the king in the inner chamber; now the king was very old, and Abishag the Shunammite was waiting on the king.
verses.1:16: Bathsheba bowed low and prostrated herself before the king. And the king said, "What do you want?"
verses.1:17: She said to him, "My lord, you yourself swore by the LORD your God to your female servant, 'Surely your son Solomon will reign after me, and he himself will sit on my throne.'
verses.1:18: And now, look, Adonijah has become king, and now, my lord the king, you do not know it.
verses.1:19: He has sacrificed oxen, fattened calves, and sheep in abundance, and he has invited all the king's sons, Abiathar the priest, and Joab the commander of the army, yet your servant Solomon he did not invite.
verses.1:20: As for you, my lord the king, the eyes of all Israel are upon you to declare to them who will sit on the throne of my lord the king after him.
verses.1:21: Otherwise it will happen, as soon as my lord the king lies down with his fathers, that I and my son Solomon will be regarded as offenders."
verses.1:22: Now look, while she was still speaking with the king, Nathan the prophet arrived.
verses.1:23: They informed the king, saying, "Here is Nathan the prophet." He entered before the king and prostrated himself to the king, with his face to the ground.
verses.1:24: Then Nathan said, "My lord the king, have you yourself said, 'Adonijah will reign after me, and he himself will sit on my throne'?
verses.1:25: For he went down today and sacrificed oxen, fattened calves, and sheep in abundance, and invited all the king's sons, the commanders of the army, and Abiathar the priest. Look, they are eating and drinking before him, and they are saying, 'Long live King Adonijah!'
verses.1:26: But me, even me your servant, and Zadok the priest, Benaiah son of Jehoiada, and your servant Solomon he has not invited.
verses.1:27: Has this matter come about from my lord the king, and you have not made known to your servant who will sit on the throne of my lord the king after him?"
verses.1:28: Then King David answered and said, "Call Bathsheba for me." So she came before the king and stood before the king.
verses.1:29: Then the king swore and said, "As the LORD lives, who redeemed my life from every distress,
verses.1:30: surely just as I swore to you by the LORD, the God of Israel, saying, 'Surely your son Solomon will reign after me, and he himself will sit on my throne in my place,' so indeed I will do this day."
verses.1:31: Then Bathsheba bowed low with her face to the earth, prostrated herself to the king, and said, "May my lord King David live forever!"
verses.1:32: King David said, "Call Zadok the priest, Nathan the prophet, and Benaiah son of Jehoiada for me." So they came in before the king.
verses.1:33: The king said to them, "Take the servants of your lord with you, set my son Solomon to ride on the mule that belongs to me, and take him down to Gihon.
verses.1:34: There let Zadok the priest and Nathan the prophet anoint him king over Israel; then blow the ram's horn and say, 'Long live King Solomon!'
verses.1:35: Then come up after him, and he will enter and sit on my throne, and he himself will reign in my place; and he is the one I have commissioned to be ruler over Israel and over Judah."
verses.1:36: Then Benaiah son of Jehoiada answered the king and said, "Amen! So may the LORD, the God of my lord the king, say.
verses.1:37: Just as the LORD was with my lord the king, so may He be with Solomon, and may He make his throne greater than the throne of my lord King David."
verses.1:38: So Zadok the priest, Nathan the prophet, Benaiah son of Jehoiada, the Cherethites, and the Pelethites went down, set Solomon to ride on King David's mule, and led him to Gihon.
verses.1:39: Then Zadok the priest took the horn of oil from the tent and anointed Solomon; and they blew the ram's horn, and all the people said, "Long live King Solomon!"
verses.1:40: And all the people went up after him, with the people playing flutes and rejoicing with great joy, so that the earth split open at their sound.
verses.1:41: Now Adonijah and all the invited guests who were with him heard it as they finished eating. When Joab heard the sound of the ram's horn, he said, "Why is there the sound of the city in an uproar?"
verses.1:42: While he was still speaking, look, Jonathan son of Abiathar the priest arrived. Adonijah said, "Come in, for you are a man of worth and you bring good news."
verses.1:43: Jonathan answered and said to Adonijah, "On the contrary, our lord King David has made Solomon king!
verses.1:44: The king has sent with him Zadok the priest, Nathan the prophet, Benaiah son of Jehoiada, the Cherethites, and the Pelethites, and they set him to ride on the king's mule.
verses.1:45: Zadok the priest and Nathan the prophet anointed him as king at Gihon, and they came up from there rejoicing, so that the city is in an uproar; that is the sound you heard.
verses.1:46: Moreover, Solomon is seated on the throne of the kingdom.
verses.1:47: Furthermore, the servants of the king came to bless our lord King David, saying, 'May God make Solomon's name better than your name, and may He make his throne greater than your throne.' And the king bowed down on the bed.
verses.1:48: And the king also spoke as follows: 'Blessed be the LORD, the God of Israel, who today has given one sitting on my throne, while my eyes see it.'"
verses.1:49: Then all the invited guests belonging to Adonijah trembled and rose up, and they went, each man on his own way.
verses.1:50: Now Adonijah was afraid of Solomon, so he got up, went, and grasped the horns of the altar.
verses.1:51: Then it was reported to Solomon, saying, "Look, Adonijah fears King Solomon, and look, he has taken hold of the horns of the altar, saying, 'Let King Solomon swear to me first that he will not put his servant to death by the sword.'"
verses.1:52: And Solomon said, "If he proves to be a man of worth, not a hair of his will fall to the ground; but if evil is found in him, he will die."
verses.1:53: Then King Solomon sent, and they took him down from the altar. He came and bowed down to King Solomon, and Solomon told him, "Go to your house."
verses.2:1: Now the days of David approached for him to die, and he commanded his son Solomon, saying,
verses.2:2: "I am going in the way of all the earth; therefore be strong and be a man.
verses.2:3: And keep the requirement of the LORD your God, to walk in His ways, to keep His statutes, His commandments, His judgments, and His testimonies, as written in the law of Moses, so that you may prosper in everything you do and everywhere you turn,
verses.2:4: in order that the LORD may establish His word that He spoke concerning me, saying, 'If your sons keep their way to walk before Me in truth with all their heart and with all their soul,' saying, 'a man will not be cut off from you from the throne of Israel.'
verses.2:5: Moreover, you yourself know what Joab son of Zeruiah did to me, what he did to the two commanders of the armies of Israel, to Abner son of Ner and to Amasa son of Jether: he killed them and shed the blood of war in peace, and he put the blood of war on his belt that was around his waist and on his sandals that were on his feet.
verses.2:6: Act according to your wisdom, then, and do not bring down his gray hair in peace to Sheol.
verses.2:7: But to the sons of Barzillai the Gileadite show loyal love, and let them be among those who eat at your table, for in this way they came near to me when I fled from before Absalom your brother.
verses.2:8: And look, with you is Shimei son of Gera, the Benjaminite from Bahurim; he cursed me with a severe curse on the day I went to Mahanaim, yet he came down to meet me at the Jordan, and I swore to him by the LORD, saying, 'I will surely not put you to death by the sword.'
verses.2:9: So now do not acquit him, for you are a wise man, and you will know what you are to do to him, and you shall bring down his gray hair with blood to Sheol."
verses.2:10: Then David lay down with his fathers and was buried in the city of David.
verses.2:11: Now the days that David reigned over Israel were forty years: in Hebron he reigned seven years, and in Jerusalem he reigned thirty-three years.
verses.2:12: And Solomon sat on the throne of his father David, and his kingdom was established very firmly.
verses.2:13: Then Adonijah son of Haggith came to Bathsheba the mother of Solomon. She said, "Is your coming in peace?" And he said, "In peace."
verses.2:14: And he said, "I have a word for you." And she said, "Speak."
verses.2:15: And he said, "You yourself know that the kingship was mine, and toward me all Israel set their faces for me to reign. However, the kingship turned around and became my brother's, for from the LORD it became his.
verses.2:16: And now I am asking one request from you; do not turn away my face." And she said to him, "Speak."
verses.2:17: And he said, "Please speak to Solomon the king, for he will not turn away your face, that he may give me Abishag the Shunammite as a wife."
verses.2:18: And Bathsheba said, "Good; I myself will speak concerning you to the king."
verses.2:19: So Bathsheba came to King Solomon to speak to him concerning Adonijah. And the king rose to meet her and bowed down to her; then he sat on his throne and had a throne placed for the mother of the king, and she sat at his right hand.
verses.2:20: Then she said, "I am asking one small request from you; do not turn away my face." And the king said to her, "Ask, my mother, for I will not turn away your face."
verses.2:21: And she said, "Let Abishag the Shunammite be given to your brother Adonijah as a wife."
verses.2:22: Then King Solomon answered and said to his mother, "And why are you asking for Abishag the Shunammite for Adonijah? Ask for him the kingship as well, for he is my older brother—for him, and for Abiathar the priest, and for Joab son of Zeruiah!"
verses.2:23: Then King Solomon swore by the LORD, saying, "Thus may God do to me, and so may He add: surely Adonijah has spoken this word at the cost of his own life!
verses.2:24: And now, as the LORD lives, who has established me and seated me on the throne of my father David, and who has made a house for me just as He spoke, surely today Adonijah shall be put to death."
verses.2:25: So King Solomon sent by the hand of Benaiah son of Jehoiada, and he struck him, and he died.
verses.2:26: And to Abiathar the priest the king said, "Go to Anathoth, to your fields, for you are a man deserving death; yet on this day I will not put you to death, because you carried the ark of the Lord GOD before my father David, and because you were afflicted in everything in which my father was afflicted."
verses.2:27: Thus Solomon expelled Abiathar from being priest to the LORD, to fulfill the word of the LORD that He had spoken concerning the house of Eli in Shiloh.
verses.2:28: Now the report reached Joab—for Joab had turned after Adonijah, though he had not turned after Absalom—and Joab fled to the tent of the LORD and grasped the horns of the altar.
verses.2:29: And it was reported to King Solomon that Joab had fled to the tent of the LORD, and there he was beside the altar. Then Solomon sent Benaiah son of Jehoiada, saying, "Go, strike him."
verses.2:30: So Benaiah came to the tent of the LORD and said to him, "This is what the king says, 'Come out!'" But he said, "No, rather I will die here." Then Benaiah brought back word to the king, saying, "This is what Joab spoke, and this is how he answered me."
verses.2:31: And the king said to him, "Do just as he has spoken: strike him and bury him, and so remove from me and from my father's house the blood that Joab shed without cause.
verses.2:32: And the LORD will bring back his blood upon his own head, because he struck two men more righteous and better than himself and killed them with the sword, while my father David did not know—Abner son of Ner, commander of the army of Israel, and Amasa son of Jether, commander of the army of Judah.
verses.2:33: Thus their blood shall come back upon the head of Joab and upon the head of his offspring forever; but for David and for his offspring and for his house and for his throne, there shall be peace forever from the LORD."
verses.2:34: Then Benaiah son of Jehoiada went up, struck him, and put him to death; and he was buried in his house in the wilderness.
verses.2:35: And the king appointed Benaiah son of Jehoiada over the army in his place, and Zadok the priest the king appointed in place of Abiathar. These were the chief deputies who were over the work for Solomon, five hundred fifty, who ruled over the people doing the work. And three times a year Solomon would offer up burnt offerings and peace offerings on the altar that he built for the LORD, and he would burn incense with it, which was before the LORD; and he completed the house.
verses.2:36: Then the king sent and summoned Shimei and said to him, "Build a house for yourself in Jerusalem and live there, and do not go out from there to this place or that.
verses.2:37: And it will come about that on the day you go out and cross the Kidron brook, you shall know for certain that you will surely die; your blood will be on your own head."
verses.2:38: And Shimei said to the king, "The word is good; just as my lord the king has spoken, so your servant will do." So Shimei lived in Jerusalem many days.
verses.2:39: Now it happened at the end of three years that two of Shimei's servants fled to Achish son of Maacah, king of Gath. And they told Shimei, saying, "Look, your servants are in Gath."
verses.2:40: Then Shimei got up, saddled his donkey, and went to Gath to Achish to search for his servants; and Shimei went and brought his servants from Gath.
verses.2:41: And it was reported to Solomon that Shimei had gone from Jerusalem to Gath and had returned.
verses.2:42: So the king sent and summoned Shimei and said to him, "Did I not make you swear by the LORD and solemnly warn you, saying, 'On the day you go out and walk to this place or that, know for certain that you will surely die'? And you said to me, 'The word is good; I have heard.'
verses.2:43: Why then have you not kept the oath of the LORD and the command that I commanded you?"
verses.2:44: And the king said to Shimei, "You yourself know all the evil that your own heart knows, which you did to my father David; therefore the LORD will bring back your evil upon your own head.
verses.2:45: Yet King Solomon is blessed, and the throne of David will remain established before the LORD forever."
verses.2:46: Then the king commanded Benaiah son of Jehoiada, and he went out and struck him, and he died. Thus the kingdom was established in the hand of Solomon. Judah and Israel were numerous, like the sand that is by the sea in abundance, eating and drinking and rejoicing. And Solomon was ruling over all the kingdoms from the River to the land of the Philistines and as far as the border of Egypt; they presented tribute and served Solomon all the days of his life. And Judah and Israel lived in security, each man beneath his vine and beneath his fig tree, from Dan as far as Beersheba, all the days of Solomon.
verses.3:2: However, the people were sacrificing at the high places, because a house had not been built for the name of the LORD until those days.
verses.3:3: And Solomon loved the LORD, walking in the statutes of David his father, except that at the high places he was sacrificing and burning incense.
verses.3:4: Then the king went to Gibeon to sacrifice there, because that was the great high place; Solomon would offer up a thousand burnt offerings on that altar.
verses.3:5: At Gibeon the LORD appeared to Solomon in a dream during the night, and God said, "Ask what I should give to you."
verses.3:6: And Solomon said, "You have shown great loyal love to Your servant David my father, just as he walked before You in truth, in righteousness, and in uprightness of heart with You; and You have kept for him this great loyal love, and have given him a son sitting on his throne as at this day.
verses.3:7: And now, LORD my God, You have made Your servant king in place of David my father, yet I am a young boy; I do not know how to go out and come in.
verses.3:8: And Your servant is in the midst of Your people whom You have chosen, a numerous people who cannot be numbered or counted for their multitude.
verses.3:9: Therefore give to Your servant a listening heart to judge Your people, to discern between good and evil; for who is able to judge this weighty people of Yours?"
verses.3:10: And the matter was good in the eyes of the Lord, that Solomon had asked for this thing.
verses.3:11: And God said to him, "Because you have asked for this thing, and have not asked for yourself many days, and have not asked for yourself wealth, and have not asked for the life of your enemies, but have asked for yourself discernment to hear justice,
verses.3:12: look, I have acted according to your words; see, I have given to you a heart that is wise and discerning, so that no one like you existed before you, and after you no one like you will arise.
verses.3:13: Moreover, what you did not ask for I have also given to you, both wealth and honor, so that no man among the kings will be like you all your days.
verses.3:14: And if you walk in My ways, to keep My statutes and My commandments, just as David your father walked, then I will prolong your days."
verses.3:15: Then Solomon woke up, and look, it was a dream. So he came to Jerusalem and stood before the ark of the covenant of the Lord, and he offered up burnt offerings, prepared peace offerings, and prepared a banquet for all his servants.
verses.3:16: At that time two women, prostitutes, came to the king and stood before him.
verses.3:17: And the one woman said, "Please, my lord, this woman and I live in one house, and I gave birth while with her in the house.
verses.3:18: And it happened on the third day after I gave birth that this woman also gave birth. We were together; no outsider was with us in the house, apart from the two of us in the house.
verses.3:19: And the son of this woman died during the night, because she lay upon him.
verses.3:20: Then she got up in the middle of the night and took my son from beside me while your maidservant was asleep; she laid him in her bosom, and her dead son she laid in my bosom.
verses.3:21: When I got up in the morning to nurse my son, look, he was dead! Then I examined him closely in the morning, and see, he was not my son whom I had borne."
verses.3:22: Then the other woman said, "No! Rather, my son is the living one, and your son is the dead one." Yet the first kept saying, "No! Rather, your son is the dead one, and my son is the living one." So they spoke before the king.
verses.3:23: Then the king said, "This one says, 'This is my son, the living one, and your son is the dead one,' while the other says, 'No! Rather, your son is the dead one, and my son is the living one.'"
verses.3:24: And the king said, "Fetch me a sword." So they brought the sword before the king.
verses.3:25: Then the king said, "Cut the living child in two, and give half to one and half to the other."
verses.3:26: Then the woman whose son was the living one spoke to the king, because her compassion was deeply stirred over her son, and she said, "Please, my lord, give her the living newborn, and certainly do not put him to death!" But the other was saying, "Neither mine nor yours shall he be; cut him!"
verses.3:27: Then the king replied and said, "Give the living newborn to her, and you must certainly not put him to death; she is his mother."
verses.3:28: And all Israel heard the judgment that the king had passed, and they were in awe before the king, for they saw that the wisdom of God was within him to do justice.
verses.4:1: And King Solomon was king over all Israel.
verses.4:2: And these were the officials whom he had: Azariah son of Zadok was the priest;
verses.4:3: Elihoreph and Ahijah, sons of Shisha, were scribes; Jehoshaphat son of Ahilud was the recorder;
verses.4:4: and Benaiah son of Jehoiada was in charge of the army, and Zadok and Abiathar were priests;
verses.4:5: and Azariah son of Nathan was in charge of the governors, and Zabud son of Nathan was a priest, the king's friend;
verses.4:6: and Ahishar was in charge of the household, and Adoniram son of Abda was in charge of the forced labor.
verses.4:7: Now Solomon had twelve governors over all Israel, who provided for the king and his household; a month in the year fell to each one to provide.
verses.4:8: And these were their names: Ben-hur, in the hill country of Ephraim;
verses.4:9: Ben-deker, in Makaz, in Shaalbim, Beth-shemesh, and Elon-beth-hanan;
verses.4:10: Ben-hesed, in Arubboth—his were Socoh and all the land of Hepher;
verses.4:11: Ben-abinadab, over all the highland of Dor—Taphath daughter of Solomon was his wife;
verses.4:12: Baana son of Ahilud, over Taanach and Megiddo and all Beth-shean, which is beside Zarethan below Jezreel, from Beth-shean to Abel-meholah, as far as beyond Jokmeam;
verses.4:13: Ben-geber, in Ramoth-gilead—his were the tent villages of Jair son of Manasseh, which are in Gilead, and his was the region of Argob, which is in Bashan, sixty large cities with walls and bars of bronze;
verses.4:14: Ahinadab son of Iddo, in Mahanaim;
verses.4:15: Ahimaaz, in Naphtali—he also took Basemath daughter of Solomon as a wife;
verses.4:16: Baana son of Hushai, in Asher and in Aloth;
verses.4:17: Shimei son of Ela, in Benjamin;
verses.4:18: Geber son of Uri, in the land of Gilead, the land of Sihon king of the Amorites and Og king of Bashan—and there was one governor who was in the land;
verses.4:19: Jehoshaphat son of Paruah, in Issachar.
verses.5:1: And these governors sustained King Solomon and everyone who came near to the table of King Solomon, each during his month; they did not let anything go missing. And they brought the barley and the straw for the horses and for the steeds to the place where he would be, each according to his assigned duty.
verses.5:2: Now Solomon's food for one day was thirty kors of fine flour and sixty kors of meal,
verses.5:3: ten fat cattle, twenty pasture-fed cattle, and a hundred sheep, apart from deer, gazelles, fallow deer, and fattened fowl.
verses.5:4: For he ruled over the entire region beyond the River, from Tiphsah as far as Gaza, over all the kings beyond the River, and he had peace on every side all around.
verses.5:9: And God gave wisdom to Solomon and exceedingly great understanding, and a breadth of heart like the sand that lies on the shore of the sea.
verses.5:10: And the wisdom of Solomon was greater than the wisdom of all the sons of the east and more than all the wisdom of Egypt.
verses.5:11: He was wiser than all humanity—than Ethan the Ezrahite, and Heman, Calcol, and Darda, the sons of Mahol—and his renown was among all the nations all around.
verses.5:12: And he spoke three thousand proverbs, and his songs numbered one thousand and five.
verses.5:13: And he spoke about the trees, from the cedar that is in Lebanon as far as the hyssop that comes out of the wall; he also spoke about beasts, about birds, about crawling creatures, and about fish.
verses.5:14: And Solomon formed a marriage alliance with Pharaoh king of Egypt; he took Pharaoh's daughter and brought her to the city of David until he finished building his own house, the house of the LORD, and the wall of Jerusalem all around. And they came from all the peoples to hear the wisdom of Solomon, from all the kings of the earth who had heard of his wisdom. Pharaoh king of Egypt had gone up, captured Gezer, and burned it with fire; he killed the Canaanites living in the city and gave it as a dowry to his daughter, Solomon's wife.
verses.5:15: Now Hiram king of Tyre sent his servants to Solomon, because he heard that they had anointed him as king in place of his father; for Hiram had been a friend to David continually.
verses.5:16: Then Solomon sent word to Hiram, saying,
verses.5:17: "You know my father David, that he could not build a house for the name of the LORD his God on account of the warfare that surrounded him, until the LORD placed them beneath the soles of my feet.
verses.5:18: And now the LORD my God has granted me rest all around; there is no adversary and no evil occurrence.
verses.5:19: Now look, I propose to build a house for the name of the LORD my God, just as the LORD spoke to my father David, saying, 'Your son, whom I will put in your place on your throne—he will build the house for My name.'
verses.5:20: So now, give the command that they cut down cedars for me from Lebanon; my servants will be with your servants, and I will give you the wages of your servants according to all that you say, for you know that there is not a man among us who knows how to cut timber like the Sidonians."
verses.5:21: And when Hiram heard Solomon's words, he rejoiced greatly and said, "Blessed be the LORD today, who has given David a wise son over this numerous people."
verses.5:22: Then Hiram sent word to Solomon, saying, "I have heard what you sent to me; I will carry out all your desire concerning cedar timber and cypress timber.
verses.5:23: My servants will bring them down from Lebanon to the sea, and I will make them into rafts on the sea as far as the place about which you send word to me; I will break them apart there, and you will carry them away. And you will carry out my desire by giving food for my household."
verses.5:24: So Hiram kept giving Solomon cedar timber and cypress timber, all that he desired.
verses.5:25: And Solomon gave Hiram twenty thousand kors of wheat as provisions for his household and twenty kors of beaten oil; in this way Solomon gave to Hiram year after year.
verses.5:26: Now the LORD gave Solomon wisdom, just as He had spoken to him. And there was peace between Hiram and Solomon, and both of them made a covenant.
verses.5:27: Then King Solomon raised forced labor from all Israel, and the forced labor amounted to thirty thousand men.
verses.5:28: And he sent them to Lebanon, ten thousand per month in rotations: they would be one month in Lebanon and two months each at home, and Adoniram was over the forced labor.
verses.5:29: Solomon also had seventy thousand carriers of burdens and eighty thousand stonecutters in the hill country,
verses.5:30: apart from Solomon's chief deputies who were over the work—three thousand three hundred who ruled over the people doing the work.
verses.5:32: So Solomon's builders, Hiram's builders, and the Gebalites shaped and prepared the timber and the stones to build the house.
verses.6:1: Now it happened in the four hundred and eightieth year after the sons of Israel went out from the land of Egypt, in the fourth year of Solomon's reign over Israel, in the month of Ziv—that is, the second month—that he began building the house for the LORD. In the fourth year the foundation of the house of the LORD was laid, in the month of Ziv. And in the eleventh year, in the month of Bul—that is, the eighth month—the house was finished in all its details and in all its specifications; thus he built it over seven years.
verses.6:2: Now the house that King Solomon built for the LORD was sixty cubits in length, twenty in width, and thirty cubits in height.
verses.6:3: And the portico in front of the main hall of the house was twenty cubits in length, across the width of the house, and ten cubits in width in front of the house.
verses.6:4: And for the house he made framed, recessed windows.
verses.6:5: And against the wall of the house he built a side structure all around, along the walls of the house all around both the main hall and the inner sanctuary, and he made side chambers all around.
verses.6:6: The lowest story was five cubits in width, the middle one six cubits in width, and the third seven cubits in width; for he put offsets on the house all around on the outside, so as not to fasten into the walls of the house.
verses.6:7: Now when the house was being built, it was built of stone completed at the quarry; neither hammers nor axe nor any iron tool was heard in the house while it was being built.
verses.6:8: The entrance to the middle side chamber was on the right side of the house, and by winding stairs they would go up to the middle story, and from the middle story to the third.
verses.6:9: So he built the house and finished it, and he roofed the house with beams and planks of cedar.
verses.6:10: And he built the side structure against the entire house, five cubits in height, and it fastened onto the house with cedar timbers.
verses.6:15: And he built the walls of the house on the inside with boards of cedar; from the floor of the house up to the walls of the ceiling he overlaid them with wood on the inside, and he overlaid the floor of the house with boards of cypress.
verses.6:16: And he built twenty cubits at the rear of the house with boards of cedar from the floor up to the walls; he built it on the inside as an inner sanctuary, as the Holy of Holies.
verses.6:17: And the house—that is, the main hall in front—measured forty cubits.
verses.6:19: And he prepared an inner sanctuary inside the house, in the innermost part, in order to place the ark of the covenant of the LORD there.
verses.6:20: Inside the inner sanctuary it was twenty cubits in length, twenty cubits in width, and twenty cubits in height; he overlaid it with pure gold, and he overlaid an altar with cedar.
verses.6:21: And Solomon overlaid the inside of the house with pure gold; he drew chains of gold across in front of the inner sanctuary, and he overlaid it with gold.
verses.6:22: The entire house he overlaid with gold until all the house was finished, and the entire altar that belonged to the inner sanctuary he overlaid with gold.
verses.6:23: And in the inner sanctuary he made two cherubim of olive wood, each ten cubits in height.
verses.6:24: One wing of the cherub was five cubits, and the other wing of the cherub was five cubits; it was ten cubits from the tip of one wing to the tip of the other.
verses.6:25: The second cherub also measured ten cubits; the two cherubim had one measurement and one shape.
verses.6:26: The height of one cherub was ten cubits, and likewise the second cherub.
verses.6:27: And he set the cherubim inside the inner house. The wings of the cherubim were outstretched so that the wing of the first touched one wall and the wing of the second cherub was touching the other wall, while their wings toward the center of the house were touching wing to wing.
verses.6:28: And he overlaid the cherubim with gold.
verses.6:29: And all around the walls of the house he carved engraved reliefs of cherubim, palm trees, and open blossoms, in both the inner and the outer rooms.
verses.6:30: And the floor of the house he overlaid with gold, in both the inner and the outer rooms.
verses.6:31: And for the entrance of the inner sanctuary he made doors of olive wood; the lintel and doorposts were a fifth part.
verses.6:32: And as for the two doors of olive wood, he carved on them reliefs of cherubim, palm trees, and open blossoms, and overlaid them with gold; he hammered the gold onto the cherubim and onto the palm trees.
verses.6:33: And in the same way he made for the entrance of the main hall doorposts of olive wood, of a fourth part,
verses.6:34: and two doors of cypress wood; the two leaves of the one door were folding, and the two leaves of the second door were folding.
verses.6:35: And he carved cherubim, palm trees, and open blossoms, and overlaid them with gold smoothed evenly over the engraved work.
verses.6:36: And he built the inner court with three courses of hewn stone and a course of cut cedar beams.
verses.7:1: Then King Solomon sent and fetched Hiram from Tyre.
verses.7:2: He was the son of a widowed woman from the tribe of Naphtali, and his father was a man of Tyre, an artisan in bronze. He was filled with wisdom, understanding, and knowledge to do every kind of work in bronze. So he came to King Solomon and carried out all his work.
verses.7:3: He fashioned the two pillars of bronze: eighteen cubits was the height of one pillar, and a cord of twelve cubits encircled the second pillar.
verses.7:4: He also made two capitals of cast bronze to place on the tops of the pillars: five cubits was the height of one capital, and five cubits was the height of the second capital.
verses.7:5: There were lattices of latticework and twisted cords of chainwork for the capitals that were on top of the pillars: seven for one capital and seven for the second capital.
verses.7:6: So he made the pillars, and two rows all around upon the one latticework to cover the capitals that were on top of the pomegranates, and he did the same for the second capital. There were capitals on the two pillars also above, close by the bulge that was beside the latticework; and the pomegranates were two hundred, in rows all around on the second capital.
verses.7:7: He erected the pillars for the portico of the main hall. He erected the right pillar and called its name Jachin, and he erected the left pillar and called its name Boaz.
verses.7:8: Now the capitals that were on top of the pillars were of lily work in the portico, four cubits. On top of the pillars was lily work, and the work of the pillars was completed.
verses.7:10: Then he made the cast sea, ten cubits from its rim to its rim, circular all around, and its height was five cubits; and a line of thirty cubits encircled it all around.
verses.7:11: Underneath its rim all around were gourds encircling it, ten to a cubit, surrounding the sea all around; the gourds were in two rows, cast in its casting.
verses.7:12: Its thickness was a handbreadth, and its rim was like the workmanship of a cup's rim, a lily blossom; it held two thousand baths.
verses.7:13: It stood on twelve oxen: three facing north, three facing west, three facing south, and three facing east. The sea was upon them above, and all their hindquarters faced inward.
verses.7:14: Then he made the ten stands of bronze: the length of each stand was four cubits, its width four cubits, and its height three cubits.
verses.7:15: This was the workmanship of the stand: they had panels, and there were panels between the frames.
verses.7:16: On the panels that were between the frames were lions, oxen, and cherubim; on the frames above was a pedestal, and beneath the lions and the oxen were wreaths of hanging work.
verses.7:17: Each stand had four bronze wheels and bronze axles, and its four feet had shoulder supports; beneath the basin the shoulder supports were cast, with wreaths beside each one.
verses.7:18: Its opening inside the crown and upward was one cubit; its opening was circular, of pedestal workmanship, a cubit and a half, and on its opening also were carvings, while their panels were square, not circular. The four wheels were underneath the panels, and the mounts of the wheels were in the stand; the height of each wheel was a cubit and a half.
verses.7:19: The workmanship of the wheels was like the workmanship of a chariot wheel: their mounts, their rims, their spokes, and their hubs were all cast.
verses.7:20: There were four shoulder supports at the four corners of each stand; its shoulder supports were part of the stand.
verses.7:21: On top of the stand was a height of half a cubit, circular all around; and on top of the stand, its stays and its panels were part of it.
verses.7:22: He engraved on the plates of its stays and on its panels cherubim, lions, and palm trees, according to the open space on each, with wreaths all around.
verses.7:23: In this way he made the ten stands: all of them had one casting, one measurement, and one form.
verses.7:24: He also made ten bronze basins: each basin held forty baths, each basin was four cubits, and there was one basin on each stand for the ten stands.
verses.7:25: He placed the stands, five on the right side of the house and five on the left side of the house; and he placed the sea on the right side of the house, toward the east, facing south.
verses.7:26: Hiram also made the basins, the shovels, and the sprinkling bowls. Thus Hiram finished doing all the work that he performed for King Solomon for the house of the LORD:
verses.7:27: two pillars, the two bowls of the capitals that were on top of the pillars, and the two lattices to cover the two bowls of the capitals that were on top of the pillars;
verses.7:28: and the four hundred pomegranates for the two lattices, two rows of pomegranates for each lattice, to cover the two bowls of the capitals that were upon the pillars;
verses.7:29: and the ten stands, and the ten basins on the stands;
verses.7:30: and the one sea, and the twelve oxen underneath the sea;
verses.7:31: and the pots, the shovels, and the sprinkling bowls. All these articles that Hiram made for King Solomon for the house of the LORD were of burnished bronze.
verses.7:32: Solomon left all the articles alone because of their exceedingly great abundance; the weight of the bronze was not ascertained.
verses.7:33: In the plain of the Jordan the king cast them, in the clay soil between Succoth and Zarethan.
verses.7:34: Then Solomon made all the articles that were in the house of the LORD: the altar of gold, and the table of gold on which was the bread of the Presence;
verses.7:35: the lampstands of pure gold, five on the right and five on the left in front of the inner sanctuary, along with the blossoms, the lamps, and the tongs of gold;
verses.7:36: the cups, the wick trimmers, the sprinkling bowls, the dishes, and the firepans of pure gold; and the hinges for the doors of the inner house, the Holy of Holies, and for the doors of the house, the main hall, of gold.
verses.7:37: So all the work that King Solomon performed for the house of the LORD was finished. Then Solomon brought in the consecrated things of his father David; the silver, the gold, and the articles he placed in the treasuries of the house of the LORD.
verses.7:38: As for his own house, Solomon built it over thirteen years, and he finished his entire house.
verses.7:39: He built the House of the Forest of Lebanon: its length was one hundred cubits, its width fifty cubits, and its height thirty cubits, upon four rows of cedar pillars, with cedar beams upon the pillars.
verses.7:40: It was paneled with cedar above over the chambers that were upon the pillars, forty-five in all, fifteen to a row.
verses.7:41: There were window frames in three rows, with window opposite window in three tiers.
verses.7:42: All the doorways and the doorposts were square in frame, and window stood opposite window in three tiers.
verses.7:43: He also made the Hall of Pillars: its length was fifty cubits and its width thirty cubits, with a portico in front of them, and pillars and a canopy in front of them.
verses.7:44: He also made the Hall of the Throne where he would judge, the Hall of Judgment; and it was paneled with cedar from floor to floor.
verses.7:45: His own house where he would dwell, in the other court inward from the hall, was of this same workmanship. He also made a house like this hall for Pharaoh's daughter, whom Solomon had married.
verses.7:46: All these were of costly stones, hewn to measure, sawed with a saw inside and outside, from the foundation to the coping, and on the outside as far as the great court.
verses.7:47: The foundation was laid with costly stones, large stones, stones of ten cubits and stones of eight cubits.
verses.7:48: And above were costly stones, hewn to measure, and cedar.
verses.7:49: The great court all around had three rows of hewn stone and a row of cedar beams, as did the inner court of the house of the LORD and the portico of the house.
verses.8:1: Then Solomon assembled the elders of Israel, all the heads of the tribes, the chiefs of the ancestral houses of the sons of Israel, to King Solomon in Jerusalem, to bring up the ark of the covenant of the LORD from the City of David, that is, Zion.
verses.8:2: And all the men of Israel assembled to King Solomon in the month of Ethanim, during the festival—that is, the seventh month.
verses.8:3: And all the elders of Israel came, and the priests lifted up the ark.
verses.8:4: They brought up the ark of the LORD, and the tent of meeting, and all the holy articles that were in the tent; and the priests and the Levites brought them up.
verses.8:5: And King Solomon and all the congregation of Israel who had gathered to him were with him before the ark, sacrificing sheep and cattle that could not be counted or numbered because of their abundance.
verses.8:6: Then the priests brought the ark of the covenant of the LORD to its place, into the inner sanctuary of the house, into the Holy of Holies, beneath the wings of the cherubim.
verses.8:7: For the cherubim were spreading their wings over the place of the ark, and the cherubim covered over the ark and over its poles from above.
verses.8:8: Now the poles were so long that the tips of the poles were visible from the Holy Place in front of the inner sanctuary, yet they were not visible outside; and they have been there to this day.
verses.8:9: Nothing was in the ark except the two stone tablets that Moses placed there at Horeb, where the LORD made a covenant with the sons of Israel when they came out from the land of Egypt.
verses.8:10: And it happened, as the priests came out from the Holy Place, that the cloud filled the house of the LORD.
verses.8:11: And the priests were unable to stand to minister on account of the cloud, because the glory of the LORD had filled the house of the LORD.
verses.8:14: Then the king turned his face around and blessed the entire assembly of Israel, while the entire assembly of Israel was standing.
verses.8:15: And he said, "Blessed is the LORD, the God of Israel, who spoke with His mouth to David my father and with His hand has fulfilled it, saying,
verses.8:16: 'From the day that I brought out My people Israel from Egypt, I did not choose a city from among all the tribes of Israel to build a house for My name to be there, yet I chose David to be over My people Israel.'
verses.8:17: And David my father had it in his heart to build a house for the name of the LORD, the God of Israel.
verses.8:18: And the LORD said to David my father, 'Since you had it in your heart to build a house for My name, you have done well that it was in your heart.
verses.8:19: However, you shall not build the house; rather, your son who comes forth from your loins, he will build the house for My name.'
verses.8:20: And the LORD has established His word that He spoke, and I have risen in the place of David my father and sit on the throne of Israel, just as the LORD spoke, and I have built the house for the name of the LORD, the God of Israel.
verses.8:21: And I have appointed a place there for the ark, in which is the covenant of the LORD that He made with our fathers when He brought them out from the land of Egypt."
verses.8:22: And Solomon stood before the altar of the LORD in the presence of the entire assembly of Israel, and he spread out his palms toward heaven.
verses.8:23: And he said, "LORD, God of Israel, there is no God like You in heaven above or on the earth beneath, keeping the covenant and loyal love for Your servants who walk before You with all their heart,
verses.8:24: You who have kept for Your servant David my father what You spoke to him; and You spoke with Your mouth, and with Your hand You have fulfilled it, as on this day.
verses.8:25: And now, LORD, God of Israel, keep for Your servant David my father what You spoke to him, saying, 'There shall not be cut off for you a man from before Me sitting on the throne of Israel, only if your sons keep their way, to walk before Me just as you have walked before Me.'
verses.8:26: And now, God of Israel, please let Your word that You spoke to Your servant David my father prove true.
verses.8:27: Yet will God truly dwell on the earth? Look, the heavens and the heaven of heavens cannot contain You—how much less this house that I have built!
verses.8:28: Yet turn toward the prayer of Your servant and toward his supplication, LORD my God, to listen to the outcry and to the prayer that Your servant is praying before You today,
verses.8:29: so that Your eyes may be open toward this house night and day, toward the place about which You said, 'My name will be there,' to listen to the prayer that Your servant prays toward this place.
verses.8:30: And listen to the supplication of Your servant and of Your people Israel when they pray toward this place. May You hear in the place of Your dwelling, in heaven; hear and forgive.
verses.8:31: If a man sins against his neighbor, and an oath is laid upon him to make him swear, and he comes and swears before Your altar in this house,
verses.8:32: then may You hear in heaven, and act and judge Your servants, condemning the wicked one by bringing his way upon his head, and vindicating the righteous one by giving to him according to his righteousness.
verses.8:33: When Your people Israel are routed before an enemy because they have sinned against You, and they return to You and acknowledge Your name, and pray and make supplication to You in this house,
verses.8:34: then may You hear in heaven, and forgive the sin of Your people Israel, and return them to the land that You gave to their fathers.
verses.8:35: When heaven is shut and there is no rain because they have sinned against You, and they pray toward this place and acknowledge Your name, and turn back from their sin when You humble them,
verses.8:36: then may You hear in heaven, and forgive the sin of Your servants and of Your people Israel, for You teach them the good way in which they are to walk, and give rain upon Your land that You gave to Your people as an inheritance.
verses.8:37: When there is famine in the land, when there is pestilence, when there is blight, mildew, locust, or caterpillar, when their enemy besieges them in the land of their gates, any affliction, any disease,
verses.8:38: whatever prayer, whatever supplication comes from any person, from all Your people Israel, as each knows the affliction of his heart and spreads out his palms toward this house,
verses.8:39: then may You hear in heaven, Your established dwelling place, and forgive and act, and give to each man according to all his ways, whose heart You know, for You alone know the heart of all the sons of mankind,
verses.8:40: so that they may fear You all the days that they live upon the face of the land that You gave to our fathers.
verses.8:41: And also concerning the foreigner who is not from Your people Israel, yet comes from a distant land for the sake of Your name—
verses.8:42: for they will hear of Your great name and Your strong hand and Your outstretched arm—when he comes and prays toward this house,
verses.8:43: may You hear in heaven, Your established dwelling place, and do according to everything for which the foreigner calls to You, so that all the peoples of the earth may know Your name, to fear You just as Your people Israel do, and to know that Your name is called upon this house that I have built.
verses.8:44: When Your people go out to war against their enemy, along the way that You send them, and they pray to the LORD toward the city that You have chosen and the house that I have built for Your name,
verses.8:45: then hear their prayer and their supplication in heaven, and uphold their cause.
verses.8:46: When they sin against You—for there is no person who does not sin—and You are angry with them and give them over before an enemy, and their captors take them captive to the land of the enemy, distant or near,
verses.8:47: yet they take it to heart in the land where they were taken captive, and turn back and make supplication to You in the land of their captors, saying, 'We have sinned and acted perversely; we have done wickedly,'
verses.8:48: and return to You with all their heart and with all their soul in the land of their enemies who took them captive, and pray to You in the direction of their land that You gave to their fathers, the city that You chose, and the house that I have built for Your name,
verses.8:49: then hear in heaven, Your established dwelling place, their prayer and their supplication, and uphold their cause,
verses.8:50: and forgive Your people who have sinned against You, and all their rebellions by which they have rebelled against You, and grant them compassion before their captors, so that they will show them compassion.
verses.8:51: For they are Your people and Your inheritance, whom You brought out from Egypt, from the midst of the iron furnace.
verses.8:52: May Your eyes be open toward the supplication of Your servant and toward the supplication of Your people Israel, to listen to them in all their calling to You.
verses.8:53: For You set them apart for Yourself as an inheritance from among all the peoples of the earth, just as You spoke by the hand of Moses Your servant when You brought out our fathers from Egypt, Lord GOD."
verses.8:54: And it happened, when Solomon had finished praying all this prayer and supplication to the LORD, that he rose from before the altar of the LORD, from kneeling upon his knees with his palms spread out toward heaven.
verses.8:55: Then he stood and blessed the entire assembly of Israel in a loud voice, saying,
verses.8:56: "Blessed is the LORD, who has given rest to His people Israel according to everything He spoke. Not a single word has failed from all His good word that He spoke by the hand of Moses His servant.
verses.8:57: May the LORD our God be with us, just as He was with our fathers; may He neither forsake us nor abandon us,
verses.8:58: to incline our heart toward Himself, to walk in all His ways and to keep His commandments and His statutes and His judgments that He commanded our fathers.
verses.8:59: And may these words of mine, by which I have made supplication before the LORD, be close to the LORD our God day and night, so that He may uphold the cause of His servant and the cause of His people Israel according to the need of each day,
verses.8:60: so that all the peoples of the earth may know that the LORD, He is God; there is no other.
verses.8:61: And let your heart be whole with the LORD our God, to walk in His statutes and to keep His commandments, as on this day."
verses.8:62: And the king and all Israel with him were offering sacrifice before the LORD.
verses.8:63: And Solomon sacrificed the sacrifice of peace offerings that he sacrificed to the LORD: twenty-two thousand cattle and one hundred twenty thousand sheep. Thus the king and all the sons of Israel dedicated the house of the LORD.
verses.8:64: On that day the king sanctified the center of the courtyard that was before the house of the LORD, because he offered there the burnt offering, and the grain offering, and the fat portions of the peace offerings, for the bronze altar that was before the LORD was too small to contain the burnt offering, and the grain offering, and the fat portions of the peace offerings.
verses.8:65: And at that time Solomon celebrated the festival, and all Israel with him, a great assembly from the entrance of Hamath to the Wadi of Egypt, before the LORD our God, seven days and seven days—fourteen days.
verses.8:66: On the eighth day he dismissed the people, and they blessed the king and went to their tents, rejoicing and glad of heart over all the goodness that the LORD had done for David His servant and for Israel His people.
verses.9:1: Now it happened, when Solomon had finished building the house of the LORD, the house of the king, and every desire of Solomon that he delighted to do,
verses.9:2: that the LORD appeared to Solomon a second time, just as He had appeared to him at Gibeon.
verses.9:3: The LORD said to him, "I have heard your prayer and your supplication that you made before Me. I have consecrated this house that you built, to set My name there forever, and My eyes and My heart will be there all the days.
verses.9:4: Now as for you, if you walk before Me as David your father walked, in wholeness of heart and in uprightness, to do according to everything that I have commanded you, and you keep My statutes and My judgments,
verses.9:5: then I will establish the throne of your kingdom over Israel forever, just as I spoke to David your father, saying, 'You will not have a man cut off from the throne of Israel.'
verses.9:6: If you indeed turn back from following Me, you and your sons, and do not keep My commandments and My statutes that I have set before you, and go and serve other gods and bow down to them,
verses.9:7: then I will cut off Israel from the face of the land that I have given them, and the house that I have consecrated for My name I will send away from My presence, and Israel will become a proverb and a taunt among all the peoples.
verses.9:8: And as for this house, exalted though it may be, everyone passing by it will be appalled and will hiss, and they will say, 'Why has the LORD done like this to this land and to this house?'
verses.9:9: And they will say, 'Because they abandoned the LORD their God, who brought their fathers out of the land of Egypt, and took hold of other gods and bowed down to them and served them; therefore the LORD has brought upon them all this calamity.'" Once Pharaoh's daughter went up from the city of David to her house that he had built for her, then he built the Millo.
verses.9:10: Now it happened at the end of twenty years, during which Solomon had built the two houses, the house of the LORD and the house of the king,
verses.9:11: Hiram king of Tyre having supplied Solomon with cedar timber and cypress timber and with gold according to all his desire, that King Solomon then gave Hiram twenty cities in the land of Galilee.
verses.9:12: Hiram went out from Tyre to see the cities that Solomon had given him, and they were not pleasing in his eyes.
verses.9:13: He said, "What cities are these that you gave me, my brother?" And he called them the land of Cabul, to this day.
verses.9:14: And Hiram sent to the king one hundred twenty talents of gold.
verses.9:26: Now King Solomon made a fleet of ships at Ezion-geber, which is beside Eloth on the shore of the Sea of Reeds, in the land of Edom.
verses.9:27: Hiram sent his servants with the fleet, seamen who knew the sea, together with the servants of Solomon.
verses.9:28: They came to Ophir, took from there four hundred twenty talents of gold, and brought it to King Solomon.
verses.10:1: Now when the queen of Sheba heard the report of Solomon regarding the name of the LORD, she came to test him with riddles.
verses.10:2: She came to Jerusalem with a very great entourage, camels carrying spices, a great quantity of gold, and precious stones. And she came to Solomon and spoke to him all that was in her heart.
verses.10:3: Solomon explained to her all her questions; there was not a single matter hidden from the king that he did not explain to her.
verses.10:4: When the queen of Sheba saw all the wisdom of Solomon and the house that he had built,
verses.10:5: the food of his table, the seating of his servants, the station of his attendants and their robes, his cupbearers, and his burnt offering that he offered up at the house of the LORD, there was no breath left in her.
verses.10:6: She said to the king, "The report that I heard in my land was true, regarding your affairs and your wisdom.
verses.10:7: Yet I did not believe the reports until I came and my eyes saw, and look, half of it was not told to me; you have added wisdom and prosperity beyond the report that I heard.
verses.10:8: Happy are your men, and happy are these servants of yours, who stand before you continually, hearing your wisdom.
verses.10:9: May the LORD your God be blessed, who delighted in you to place you on the throne of Israel! Because the LORD loves Israel forever, He has appointed you king to carry out justice and righteousness."
verses.10:10: She gave to the king one hundred twenty talents of gold, spices in very great abundance, and precious stones; never again did spices come in such quantity as those that the queen of Sheba gave to King Solomon.
verses.10:11: Moreover, Hiram's fleet, which carried gold from Ophir, brought from Ophir a very great quantity of almug timber and precious stones.
verses.10:12: From the almug timber the king made supports for the house of the LORD and for the house of the king, along with lyres and harps for the singers. No such almug timber has come, nor has any been seen, to this day.
verses.10:13: King Solomon gave to the queen of Sheba all her desire that she asked for, besides what he gave her according to the bounty of King Solomon. Then she turned and went to her land, she and her servants.
verses.10:14: The weight of the gold that came to Solomon in a single year was six hundred sixty-six talents of gold,
verses.10:15: besides that of the traveling merchants and the commerce of the traders, and of all the kings of the mixed peoples and the governors of the land.
verses.10:16: King Solomon made two hundred large shields of beaten gold; six hundred shekels of gold went onto each large shield.
verses.10:17: He also made three hundred shields of beaten gold; three minas of gold went onto each shield. And the king placed them in the House of the Forest of Lebanon.
verses.10:18: The king also made a large ivory throne and overlaid it with refined gold.
verses.10:19: The throne had six steps, and the throne had a rounded top at its back, with armrests on either side of the place of the seat, and two lions standing beside the armrests.
verses.10:20: Twelve lions stood there on the six steps, on one side and on the other; nothing like this had been made for any kingdom.
verses.10:21: All the drinking vessels of King Solomon were gold, and all the vessels of the House of the Forest of Lebanon were pure gold. None was of silver; it was not reckoned as anything in the days of Solomon.
verses.10:22: Now this is the account of the forced labor that King Solomon levied to build the house of the LORD, his house, the Millo, the wall of Jerusalem, Hazor, Megiddo, and Gezer. Solomon built Gezer, Lower Beth-horon, Baalath, Tadmor in the wilderness in the land, all the storage cities that belonged to Solomon, the chariot cities, the cities for horsemen, and Solomon's desire that he desired to build in Jerusalem, in Lebanon, and in all the land of his dominion. As for all the people who were left of the Amorites, the Hittites, the Perizzites, the Hivites, and the Jebusites, who were not of the sons of Israel—their descendants who were left after them in the land, whom the sons of Israel had not been able to devote to destruction—Solomon levied them as forced laborers, to this day. Yet of the sons of Israel Solomon made no one a slave, for they were the men of war, his servants, his commanders, his captains, and the commanders of his chariots and his horsemen. For the king had a fleet of Tarshish at sea with the fleet of Hiram; once every three years the fleet of Tarshish would come carrying gold and silver, ivory, apes, and peacocks.
verses.10:23: Thus King Solomon grew greater than all the kings of the earth in wealth and in wisdom.
verses.10:24: And the whole earth kept seeking the presence of Solomon to hear his wisdom, which God had placed in his heart.
verses.10:25: And each of them would bring his tribute—articles of silver and articles of gold, garments, weapons, spices, horses, and mules—a set amount year by year.
verses.10:26: Solomon had forty thousand stalls of horses for his chariots and twelve thousand horsemen. And Solomon assembled chariots and horsemen; he had one thousand four hundred chariots and twelve thousand horsemen, and he stationed them in the chariot cities and with the king in Jerusalem.
verses.10:27: The king made silver like stones in Jerusalem, and cedars he made as abundant as the sycamores that are in the lowland.
verses.10:28: Now the export of horses for Solomon was from Egypt and from Kue; the king's traders would acquire them from Kue for a price.
verses.10:29: A chariot came up and went out from Egypt for six hundred shekels of silver, and a horse for one hundred fifty; and in the same way these were exported by their hand to all the kings of the Hittites and to the kings of Aram.
verses.11:1: Now King Solomon loved many foreign women, as well as the daughter of Pharaoh: Moabite, Ammonite, Edomite, Sidonian, and Hittite women.
verses.11:2: From the nations concerning which the LORD had said to the sons of Israel, "You shall not go among them, and they shall not come among you; surely they will turn your heart after their gods"—to these Solomon clung in love.
verses.11:4: And it happened at the time of Solomon's old age that his wives turned his heart after other gods, and his heart was not whole with the LORD his God like the heart of his father David.
verses.11:5: Then Solomon built a high place for Chemosh, the detestable thing of Moab, on the mountain facing Jerusalem, and for Molech, the detestable thing of the sons of Ammon.
verses.11:6: And Solomon went after Ashtoreth, the goddess of the Sidonians, and after Milcom, the detestable thing of the Ammonites.
verses.11:7: And so he did for all his foreign wives, who burned incense and sacrificed to their gods.
verses.11:8: And Solomon did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD, and he did not follow the LORD fully like David his father.
verses.11:9: So the LORD grew angry with Solomon, because his heart had turned away from the LORD, the God of Israel, who had appeared to him twice.
verses.11:10: And He had commanded him concerning this matter, not to go after other gods, yet he did not keep what the LORD had commanded.
verses.11:11: Then the LORD said to Solomon, "Because this has been with you, and you have not kept My covenant and My statutes that I commanded you, I will certainly tear the kingdom away from you and give it to your servant.
verses.11:12: However, I will not do it in your days, for the sake of David your father; out of the hand of your son I will tear it.
verses.11:13: Yet I will not tear away the whole kingdom; I will give one tribe to your son for the sake of David My servant and for the sake of Jerusalem, which I have chosen."
verses.11:14: Then the LORD raised up an adversary against Solomon, Hadad the Edomite; he was of the king's offspring in Edom. And God raised up an adversary against him, Rezon the son of Eliada, who had fled from his master Hadadezer, king of Zobah. He gathered men to himself and became commander of a raiding band when David killed them; and they went to Damascus and settled in it, and they reigned in Damascus.
verses.11:15: Now it happened when David was in Edom, as Joab the commander of the army went up to bury the fallen, that he struck down every male in Edom.
verses.11:16: For Joab and all Israel stayed there six months, until he had cut off every male in Edom.
verses.11:17: But Hadad fled, he and some Edomite men from his father's servants with him, to go to Egypt, while Hadad was a young boy.
verses.11:18: They arose from Midian and came to Paran; they took men with them from Paran and came to Egypt, to Pharaoh king of Egypt, who gave him a house, ordered food for him, and gave him land.
verses.11:19: And Hadad found great favor in the eyes of Pharaoh, so that he gave him as a wife the sister of his own wife, the sister of Tahpenes the queen.
verses.11:20: And the sister of Tahpenes bore him his son Genubath, whom Tahpenes weaned within Pharaoh's house; and Genubath was in Pharaoh's house among the sons of Pharaoh.
verses.11:21: Now Hadad heard in Egypt that David had slept with his fathers and that Joab the commander of the army had died; so Hadad said to Pharaoh, "Send me away, so that I may go to my land."
verses.11:22: Then Pharaoh said to him, "What are you lacking with me, that now you are seeking to go to your land?" And he said, "Nothing; rather, be sure to send me away."
verses.11:25: And he was an adversary to Israel all the days of Solomon, along with the harm that Hadad did; and he loathed Israel and reigned over Aram.
verses.11:26: Now Jeroboam the son of Nebat, an Ephraimite from Zeredah—his mother's name was Zeruah, a widow—was a servant of Solomon, and he lifted up a hand against the king.
verses.11:27: And this was the reason he lifted up a hand against the king: Solomon built the Millo and closed up the breach of the city of David his father.
verses.11:28: Now the man Jeroboam was a mighty man of strength; and Solomon saw that the young man worked diligently, so he appointed him over all the labor burden of the house of Joseph.
verses.11:29: And it happened at that time, when Jeroboam went out from Jerusalem, that Ahijah the Shilonite, the prophet, found him on the road. Now he was wrapped in a new cloak, and the two of them were alone in the field.
verses.11:30: Then Ahijah seized the new cloak that was on him and tore it into twelve pieces.
verses.11:31: And he said to Jeroboam, "Take for yourself ten pieces, for this is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: 'Look, I am about to tear the kingdom out of the hand of Solomon, and I will give you the ten tribes,
verses.11:32: while the one tribe shall belong to him, for the sake of My servant David and for the sake of Jerusalem, the city that I have chosen out of all the tribes of Israel,
verses.11:33: because they have forsaken Me and bowed down to Ashtoreth, the goddess of the Sidonians, to Chemosh, the god of Moab, and to Milcom, the god of the sons of Ammon, and have not walked in My ways, to do what is right in My eyes and My statutes and My judgments, as David his father did.
verses.11:34: Yet I will not take the whole kingdom out of his hand, but I will appoint him as prince all the days of his life, for the sake of David My servant whom I chose, who kept My commandments and My statutes.
verses.11:35: But I will take the kingship out of the hand of his son and give it to you—the ten tribes.
verses.11:36: And to his son I will give one tribe, so that David My servant may have a lamp before Me always in Jerusalem, the city that I have chosen for Myself to set My name there.
verses.11:37: And as for you, I will take you, and you will reign over everything that your soul desires, and you will be king over Israel.
verses.11:38: And it shall be that if you listen to all that I command you, and walk in My ways, and do what is right in My eyes by keeping My statutes and My commandments, as David My servant did, then I will be with you and build for you a steadfast house, just as I built for David, and I will give Israel to you.'"
verses.11:40: So Solomon sought to put Jeroboam to death, but Jeroboam arose and fled to Egypt, to Shishak king of Egypt, and he was in Egypt until the death of Solomon.
verses.11:41: As for the rest of the deeds of Solomon, and all that he did, and his wisdom, are they not written in the book of the deeds of Solomon?
verses.11:42: And the days that Solomon reigned in Jerusalem over all Israel were forty years.
verses.11:43: And Solomon slept with his fathers and was buried in the city of David his father, and his son Rehoboam reigned in his place.
verses.12:1: And Rehoboam went to Shechem, because all Israel had come to Shechem to make him king.
verses.12:3: And they sent and called for him, and Jeroboam and all the assembly of Israel came and spoke to Rehoboam, saying,
verses.12:4: "Your father made our yoke harsh; as for you, now lighten your father's harsh labor and his heavy yoke that he laid on us, and we will serve you."
verses.12:5: And he said to them, "Go away for three more days, then return to me." So the people went away.
verses.12:6: Then King Rehoboam consulted with the elders who had stood before his father Solomon while he was alive, saying, "How do you advise bringing back an answer to this people?"
verses.12:7: And they spoke to him, saying, "If today you will be a servant to this people and serve them, and answer them and speak good words to them, then they will be servants to you always."
verses.12:8: But he abandoned the counsel of the elders that they had counseled him, and consulted with the young men who had grown up with him and who stood before him.
verses.12:9: And he said to them, "What do you advise that we bring back as an answer to this people who have spoken to me, saying, 'Lighten the yoke that your father put on us'?"
verses.12:10: And the young men who had grown up with him spoke to him, saying, "Thus you shall say to this people who spoke to you, saying, 'Your father made our yoke heavy, but you, lighten it from upon us'—thus you shall speak to them: 'My little finger is thicker than my father's loins.
verses.12:11: And now, my father loaded a heavy yoke upon you, yet I will add to your yoke; my father disciplined you with whips, yet I will discipline you with scorpions.'"
verses.12:12: So Jeroboam and all the people came to Rehoboam on the third day, just as the king had spoken, saying, "Return to me on the third day."
verses.12:13: And the king answered the people harshly, and he abandoned the counsel of the elders that they had counseled him.
verses.12:14: And he spoke to them according to the counsel of the young men, saying, "My father made your yoke heavy, yet I will add to your yoke; my father disciplined you with whips, yet I will discipline you with scorpions."
verses.12:15: So the king did not listen to the people, for it was a turn of events from the LORD, in order to establish His word that the LORD had spoken by the hand of Ahijah the Shilonite to Jeroboam the son of Nebat.
verses.12:16: And all Israel saw that the king had not listened to them, so the people brought back an answer to the king, saying, "What share do we have in David? And there is no inheritance in the son of Jesse! To your tents, Israel! Now see to your own house, David!" So Israel went to their tents.
verses.12:18: Then King Rehoboam sent Adoram, who was over the forced labor, and all Israel stoned him with stones, and he died. And King Rehoboam exerted himself to mount the chariot to flee to Jerusalem.
verses.12:19: And Israel has been in revolt against the house of David to this day.
verses.12:20: Now it happened when all Israel heard that Jeroboam had returned, that they sent and called him to the congregation and made him king over all Israel. None followed the house of David except the tribe of Judah alone.
verses.12:21: And Rehoboam came to Jerusalem and assembled all the house of Judah and the tribe of Benjamin, one hundred eighty thousand chosen fighting men, to fight against the house of Israel, to restore the kingship to Rehoboam the son of Solomon.
verses.12:22: Then the word of God came to Shemaiah, the man of God, saying,
verses.12:23: "Say to Rehoboam the son of Solomon, king of Judah, and to all the house of Judah and Benjamin, and to the rest of the people, saying,
verses.12:24: 'This is what the LORD says: You shall not go up, nor shall you fight against your brothers, the sons of Israel. Return, every man to his house, for this matter has come about from Me.'" So they listened to the word of the LORD and turned back to depart according to the word of the LORD. At that time Abijah the son of Jeroboam fell ill. And Jeroboam said to his wife, "Arise now and disguise yourself so that they will not know that you are the wife of Jeroboam, and go to Shiloh. Look, Ahijah the prophet is there, the one who spoke about me to be king over this people. Take in your hand ten loaves of bread, cakes, and a jar of honey, and go to him. He will tell you what will happen to the boy." And the wife of Jeroboam did so; she arose and went to Shiloh, and came to the house of Ahijah. Now Ahijah could not see, because his eyes had grown dim from his old age. Now the LORD had said to Ahijah, "Look, the wife of Jeroboam is coming to inquire a word from you concerning her son, for he is ill. Thus and thus you shall speak to her; and it will be, as she enters, that she will pretend to be a stranger." And it happened when Ahijah heard the sound of her feet coming in at the doorway, that he said, "Come in, wife of Jeroboam! Why is it that you are pretending to be a stranger? For I have been sent to you with harsh news."
verses.12:25: Then Jeroboam built Shechem in the hill country of Ephraim and settled in it; then he went out from there and built Penuel.
verses.12:26: Then Jeroboam said in his heart, "Now the kingdom will return to the house of David.
verses.12:27: If this people goes up to offer sacrifices in the house of the LORD in Jerusalem, then the heart of this people will return to their lord, to Rehoboam king of Judah, and they will kill me and return to Rehoboam king of Judah."
verses.12:28: Then the king sought counsel and made two golden calves, and he said to them, "It is too much for you to go up to Jerusalem; here are your gods, Israel, who brought you up from the land of Egypt."
verses.12:29: He placed the one in Bethel, and the other he set in Dan.
verses.12:30: Now this thing became a sin, for the people went before the one as far as Dan.
verses.12:31: And he made a house of high places, and he made priests from every part of the people who were not of the sons of Levi.
verses.12:32: And Jeroboam instituted a festival in the eighth month, on the fifteenth day of the month, like the festival that is in Judah, and he went up to the altar; so he did in Bethel, sacrificing to the calves that he had made. And he stationed in Bethel the priests of the high places that he had made.
verses.12:33: And he went up to the altar that he had made in Bethel on the fifteenth day in the eighth month, in the month that he had devised out of his own heart; and he instituted a festival for the sons of Israel and went up to the altar to burn incense.
verses.13:1: Now look, a man of God came from Judah by the word of the LORD to Bethel, and Jeroboam was standing beside the altar to burn incense.
verses.13:2: He cried out against the altar by the word of the LORD and said, "Altar, altar, this is what the LORD says: 'Look, a son will be born to the house of David, Josiah is his name; and on you he will sacrifice the priests of the high places who burn incense on you, and human bones will be burned on you.'"
verses.13:3: And on that day he gave a sign, saying, "This is the sign that the LORD has spoken: Look, the altar will be split open, and the ashes that are on it will be spilled out."
verses.13:4: When the king heard the word of the man of God that he cried out against the altar in Bethel, Jeroboam stretched out his hand from the altar, saying, "Seize him!" Then his hand that he had stretched out against him withered, and he could not bring it back to himself.
verses.13:5: The altar also was split open, and the ashes were spilled out from the altar, according to the sign that the man of God had given by the word of the LORD.
verses.13:6: Then the king answered and said to the man of God, "Please implore the favor of the LORD your God and pray on my behalf, so that my hand may be restored to me." So the man of God implored the favor of the LORD, and the king's hand was restored to him, and it became as it was at first.
verses.13:7: Then the king spoke to the man of God, "Come with me to the house and refresh yourself, and I will give you a gift."
verses.13:8: But the man of God said to the king, "Even if you give me half of your house, I will not go with you, and I will not eat bread or drink water in this place.
verses.13:9: For in this way I was commanded by the word of the LORD, saying, 'You must not eat bread and you must not drink water, and you must not return by the road that you traveled.'"
verses.13:10: So he went by another road, and he did not return by the road on which he had come to Bethel.
verses.13:11: Now a certain old prophet was living in Bethel; and his son came and recounted to him every deed that the man of God had done that day in Bethel, and the words that he had spoken to the king they also recounted to their father.
verses.13:12: Their father spoke to them, "By which road did he go?" Now his sons had seen the road on which the man of God who came from Judah had gone.
verses.13:13: Then he said to his sons, "Saddle the donkey for me." So they saddled the donkey for him, and he rode on it.
verses.13:14: He went after the man of God and found him sitting under the terebinth tree. And he said to him, "Are you the man of God who came from Judah?" And he said, "I am."
verses.13:15: Then he said to him, "Come with me to the house and eat bread."
verses.13:16: He said, "I cannot return with you or go in with you, and I will not eat bread nor drink water with you in this place.
verses.13:17: For a word came to me by the word of the LORD, 'You must not eat bread and you must not drink water there; you must not return to travel by the road on which you went.'"
verses.13:18: He said to him, "I too am a prophet like you, and an angel spoke to me by the word of the LORD, saying, 'Bring him back with you to your house so that he may eat bread and drink water.'" He lied to him.
verses.13:19: So he turned back with him, and he ate bread in his house and drank water.
verses.13:20: While they were sitting at the table, the word of the LORD came to the prophet who had brought him back.
