verses.13:21: He cried out to the man of God who had come from Judah, saying, "This is what the LORD says: Because you have rebelled against the command of the LORD and have not kept the commandment that the LORD your God commanded you,
verses.13:22: but turned back and ate bread and drank water in the place about which He spoke to you, 'Do not eat bread and do not drink water,' your corpse will not come to the tomb of your fathers."
verses.13:23: After he had eaten bread and after he had drunk, he saddled the donkey for him, for the prophet whom he had brought back.
verses.13:24: So he departed, and a lion met him on the road and killed him. His corpse was thrown on the road, while the donkey stood beside it, and the lion stood beside the corpse.
verses.13:25: Look, men were passing by, and they saw the corpse thrown on the road and the lion standing beside the corpse. They came and spoke about it in the city where the old prophet lived.
verses.13:26: When the prophet who had brought him back from the road heard, he said, "It is the man of God who rebelled against the command of the LORD; so the LORD handed him over to the lion, which mauled him and killed him, according to the word of the LORD that He spoke to him."
verses.13:28: He went and found his corpse thrown on the road, with the donkey and the lion standing beside the corpse. The lion had not eaten the corpse, nor had it mauled the donkey.
verses.13:29: Then the prophet lifted up the corpse of the man of God, laid it on the donkey, and brought it back; and he came into the city of the old prophet to mourn and to bury him.
verses.13:30: He laid his corpse in his own tomb, and they mourned over him, "Alas, my brother!"
verses.13:31: After he had buried him, he said to his sons, "When I die, bury me in the tomb where the man of God is buried; lay my bones beside his bones.
verses.13:32: For the word that he cried out by the word of the LORD against the altar that is in Bethel and against all the houses of the high places that are in the cities of Samaria will surely come about."
verses.13:33: After this event Jeroboam did not turn back from his evil way, but again he made priests of the high places from every part of the people; whoever wished, he would consecrate him so that he became one of the priests of the high places.
verses.13:34: And through this matter it became the sin of the house of Jeroboam, so as to wipe it out and destroy it from the face of the earth.
verses.14:21: Now Rehoboam son of Solomon reigned in Judah. Rehoboam was forty-one years old when he began to reign, and he reigned seventeen years in Jerusalem, the city that the LORD had chosen from all the tribes of Israel to place His name there. His mother's name was Naamah the Ammonite.
verses.14:22: Judah did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD, and they provoked Him to jealousy more than all that their fathers had done, with the sins that they committed.
verses.14:23: They too built for themselves high places, standing stones, and Asherah poles on every high hill and beneath every flourishing tree.
verses.14:24: Male shrine prostitutes were also in the land; they acted in accordance with all the abominations of the nations that the LORD had dispossessed before the sons of Israel.
verses.14:25: In the fifth year of King Rehoboam, Shishak king of Egypt marched up against Jerusalem.
verses.14:26: He took the treasures of the house of the LORD and the treasures of the king's house; he took all of it, and he took all the shields of gold that Solomon had made.
verses.14:27: Then King Rehoboam made shields of bronze in their place and entrusted them to the charge of the commanders of the guards who watched over the entrance of the king's house.
verses.14:28: Whenever the king went into the house of the LORD, the guards would carry them and bring them back to the chamber of the guards.
verses.14:29: Now the rest of the deeds of Rehoboam and everything that he did, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah?
verses.14:30: And there was war between Rehoboam and Jeroboam all the time.
verses.14:31: Then Rehoboam lay down with his fathers and was buried with his fathers in the city of David. His mother's name was Naamah the Ammonite. And Abijam his son reigned in his place.
verses.15:1: And in the eighteenth year of King Jeroboam son of Nebat, Abijam began to reign over Judah.
verses.15:2: He reigned three years in Jerusalem, and the name of his mother was Maacah, daughter of Abishalom.
verses.15:3: He walked in all the sins of his father that he had done before him, and his heart was not wholly with the LORD his God, like the heart of David his father.
verses.15:4: Yet for David's sake the LORD his God gave him a lamp in Jerusalem, to raise up his son after him and to make Jerusalem stand firm,
verses.15:5: because David did what was right in the eyes of the LORD and did not turn aside from anything that He commanded him all the days of his life, except in the matter of Uriah the Hittite.
verses.15:7: And the rest of the deeds of Abijam and all that he did, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah? And there was war between Abijam and Jeroboam.
verses.15:8: And Abijam lay down with his fathers, and they buried him in the city of David, and his son Asa began to reign in his place.
verses.15:9: And in the twentieth year of Jeroboam king of Israel, Asa began to reign as king of Judah.
verses.15:10: And he reigned forty-one years in Jerusalem, and the name of his mother was Maacah, daughter of Abishalom.
verses.15:11: And Asa did what was right in the eyes of the LORD, like David his father.
verses.15:12: He banished the male cult prostitutes from the land and removed all the idols that his fathers had made.
verses.15:13: Moreover, he removed Maacah his mother from being queen mother, because she had made a repulsive image for Asherah; and Asa cut down her repulsive image and burned it in the Kidron Valley.
verses.15:14: But the high places were not removed; nevertheless, Asa's heart was wholly with the LORD all his days.
verses.15:15: He brought in the dedicated things of his father and the dedicated things of the house of the LORD, silver and gold and vessels.
verses.15:16: And there was war between Asa and Baasha king of Israel all their days.
verses.15:17: Baasha king of Israel went up against Judah and built Ramah, so as not to let anyone go out or come in to Asa king of Judah.
verses.15:18: Then Asa took all the silver and the gold remaining in the treasuries of the house of the LORD and the treasuries of the king's house, and he put them into the hand of his servants. And King Asa sent them to Ben-hadad son of Tabrimmon, son of Hezion, king of Aram, who resided in Damascus, saying,
verses.15:19: "Let there be a covenant between me and you, as between my father and your father. Look, I have sent you a bribe of silver and gold; go, break your covenant with Baasha king of Israel, so that he will withdraw from me."
verses.15:20: Ben-hadad listened to King Asa and sent the commanders of his armies against the cities of Israel, and he struck Ijon, Dan, Abel-beth-maacah, and all Chinneroth, along with all the land of Naphtali.
verses.15:21: When Baasha heard of it, he stopped building Ramah and remained in Tirzah.
verses.15:22: Then King Asa issued a proclamation to all Judah, with no one exempt, and they carried away the stones of Ramah and its timber with which Baasha had been building; and with them King Asa built Geba of Benjamin and Mizpah.
verses.15:23: And the rest of all the deeds of Asa, and all his might, and all that he did, and the cities that he built, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah? Yet in the time of his old age he became diseased in his feet.
verses.15:24: And Asa lay down with his fathers and was buried with his fathers in the city of David his father, and his son Jehoshaphat began to reign in his place.
verses.15:25: And Nadab son of Jeroboam began to reign over Israel in the second year of Asa king of Judah, and he reigned over Israel two years.
verses.15:26: He did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD and walked in the way of his father and in his sin by which he caused Israel to sin.
verses.15:27: Then Baasha son of Ahijah, of the house of Issachar, conspired against him; and Baasha struck him down at Gibbethon, which belonged to the Philistines, while Nadab and all Israel were laying siege to Gibbethon.
verses.15:28: So Baasha put him to death in the third year of Asa king of Judah, and began to reign in his place.
verses.15:29: As soon as he became king, he struck down the entire house of Jeroboam; he did not leave to Jeroboam anyone who breathed, until he had destroyed it, according to the word of the LORD that He spoke by the hand of His servant Ahijah the Shilonite,
verses.15:30: because of the sins of Jeroboam that he sinned and by which he caused Israel to sin, because of his provocation by which he provoked the LORD, the God of Israel, to anger.
verses.15:31: And the rest of the deeds of Nadab and all that he did, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel?
verses.15:33: In the third year of Asa king of Judah, Baasha son of Ahijah became king over all Israel in Tirzah for twenty-four years.
verses.15:34: He did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD and walked in the way of Jeroboam and in his sin by which he caused Israel to sin.
verses.16:1: And the word of the LORD came to Jehu son of Hanani against Baasha, saying,
verses.16:2: "Because I lifted you up from the dust and made you ruler over My people Israel, yet you walked in the way of Jeroboam and caused My people Israel to sin, to provoke Me to anger with their sins,
verses.16:3: look, I am about to sweep away Baasha and his house, and I will make your house like the house of Jeroboam son of Nebat.
verses.16:4: Anyone belonging to Baasha who dies in the city, the dogs will eat; and anyone belonging to him who dies in the field, the birds of the sky will eat."
verses.16:5: And the rest of the deeds of Baasha, and what he did, and his might, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel?
verses.16:6: And Baasha lay down with his fathers and was buried in Tirzah, and his son Elah began to reign in his place.
verses.16:7: Moreover, by the hand of Jehu son of Hanani the prophet, the word of the LORD came against Baasha and against his house, both because of all the evil that he did in the eyes of the LORD, provoking Him to anger with the work of his hands so as to be like the house of Jeroboam, and because he struck it down.
verses.16:8: In the twenty-sixth year of Asa king of Judah, Elah son of Baasha became king over Israel in Tirzah for two years.
verses.16:9: And his servant Zimri, commander of half the chariots, conspired against him while he was in Tirzah, drinking himself drunk in the house of Arza, who was over the household in Tirzah.
verses.16:10: And Zimri came in, struck him down, and put him to death in the twenty-seventh year of Asa king of Judah, and began to reign in his place.
verses.16:11: When he became king, as soon as he sat on his throne, he struck down the entire house of Baasha; he did not leave to him anyone who urinates against a wall, neither his close kinsmen nor his friends.
verses.16:12: Thus Zimri destroyed the entire house of Baasha, according to the word of the LORD that He spoke against Baasha by the hand of Jehu the prophet,
verses.16:13: on account of all the sins of Baasha and the sins of his son Elah, which they sinned and by which they caused Israel to sin, provoking the LORD, the God of Israel, to anger with their empty idols.
verses.16:14: And the rest of the deeds of Elah and all that he did, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel?
verses.16:15: In the twenty-seventh year of Asa king of Judah, Zimri reigned seven days in Tirzah, while the people were encamped against Gibbethon, which belonged to the Philistines.
verses.16:16: And the people who were encamped heard it said, "Zimri has conspired and has also struck down the king." So all Israel made Omri, commander of the army, king over Israel on that day in the camp.
verses.16:17: Then Omri and all Israel with him went up from Gibbethon and laid siege to Tirzah.
verses.16:18: When Zimri saw that the city had been captured, he went into the citadel of the king's house and burned the king's house over himself with fire, and died,
verses.16:19: because of his sins that he sinned, in doing what was evil in the eyes of the LORD, walking in the way of Jeroboam and in his sin that he committed, causing Israel to sin.
verses.16:20: And the rest of the deeds of Zimri, and his conspiracy that he conspired, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel?
verses.16:21: Then the people of Israel were divided in half: half of the people followed Tibni son of Ginath to make him king, and the other half followed Omri.
verses.16:22: But the people who followed Omri prevailed over the people who followed Tibni son of Ginath; so Tibni died, and Omri became king.
verses.16:23: In the thirty-first year of Asa king of Judah, Omri became king over Israel for twelve years; in Tirzah he reigned six years.
verses.16:24: He bought the hill of Samaria from Shemer for two talents of silver; and he built up the hill, and called the name of the city that he built Samaria, after the name of Shemer, the owner of the hill.
verses.16:25: And Omri did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD, and did more evil than all who were before him.
verses.16:26: He walked in all the way of Jeroboam son of Nebat and in his sin by which he caused Israel to sin, provoking the LORD, the God of Israel, to anger with their empty idols.
verses.16:27: And the rest of the deeds of Omri that he did, and his might that he showed, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel?
verses.16:28: And Omri lay down with his fathers and was buried in Samaria, and his son Ahab began to reign in his place.
verses.16:29: And Ahab son of Omri began to reign over Israel in the thirty-eighth year of Asa king of Judah, and Ahab son of Omri reigned over Israel in Samaria twenty-two years.
verses.16:30: And Ahab son of Omri did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD, more than all who were before him.
verses.16:31: And as if it had been a light thing for him to walk in the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, he took as wife Jezebel daughter of Ethbaal, king of the Sidonians, and he went and served Baal and bowed down to him.
verses.16:32: He set up an altar for Baal in the house of Baal that he built in Samaria.
verses.16:33: And Ahab made the Asherah, and Ahab did yet more to provoke the LORD, the God of Israel, to anger than all the kings of Israel who had been before him.
verses.16:34: In his days Hiel the Bethelite built Jericho; at the cost of Abiram his firstborn he laid its foundation, and at the cost of Segub his youngest he set up its gates, according to the word of the LORD that He spoke by the hand of Joshua son of Nun.
verses.17:1: And Elijah the Tishbite, from among the settlers of Gilead, said to Ahab, "As the LORD, the God of Israel, lives, before whom I stand, there will be no dew or rain during these years, except according to my word."
verses.17:2: Then the word of the LORD came to him, saying,
verses.17:3: "Depart from here, turn eastward, and hide yourself in the Wadi Cherith, which lies east of the Jordan.
verses.17:4: And it will be that you will drink from the wadi, and I have commanded the ravens to sustain you there."
verses.17:5: So he went and acted according to the word of the LORD; he went and stayed in the Wadi Cherith, which lies east of the Jordan.
verses.17:6: And the ravens kept bringing him bread and meat in the morning, and bread and meat in the evening, and he would drink from the wadi.
verses.17:7: Then it happened after some days that the wadi dried up, because there had been no rain in the land.
verses.17:8: Then the word of the LORD came to him, saying,
verses.17:9: "Rise, go to Zarephath, which belongs to Sidon, and stay there. Look, I have commanded a widow there to sustain you."
verses.17:10: So he rose and went to Zarephath. When he came to the entrance of the city, look, a widow was there gathering sticks. He called out to her and said, "Please get me a little water in a vessel so that I may drink."
verses.17:11: As she went to get it, he called out to her and said, "Please bring me a morsel of bread in your hand."
verses.17:12: But she said, "As the LORD your God lives, I have no baked cake, only a handful of flour in the jar and a little oil in the flask. Look, I am gathering two sticks so that I may go in and prepare it for myself and my son, that we may eat it and die."
verses.17:13: Then Elijah said to her, "Do not be afraid; go, do as you said. Only make a small cake for me from it first and bring it out to me, and afterward make some for yourself and your son.
verses.17:14: For this is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: 'The jar of flour will not be used up, and the flask of oil will not run short, until the day the LORD gives rain on the face of the ground.'"
verses.17:15: So she went and acted according to the word of Elijah, and she and he and her household ate for days.
verses.17:16: The jar of flour was not used up, and the flask of oil did not run short, according to the word of the LORD that He spoke through Elijah.
verses.17:17: Now it happened after these things that the son of the woman, the owner of the house, fell ill, and his illness became very severe, until no breath remained in him.
verses.17:18: So she said to Elijah, "What is there between me and you, man of God? Have you come to me to call my iniquity to remembrance and to put my son to death?"
verses.17:19: And he said to her, "Give me your son." Then he took him from her arms, carried him up to the upper room where he was staying, and laid him on his bed.
verses.17:20: He called out to the LORD and said, "LORD my God, have You also brought calamity upon the widow with whom I am lodging, by putting her son to death?"
verses.17:21: Then he stretched himself out over the child three times, and called out to the LORD and said, "LORD my God, please let the life of this child return into him."
verses.17:22: And the LORD listened to the voice of Elijah, and the life of the child returned into him, and he lived.
verses.17:23: Then Elijah took the child and brought him down from the upper room into the house, and gave him to his mother. And Elijah said, "See, your son is alive!"
verses.17:24: Then the woman said to Elijah, "Now indeed I know that you are a man of God, and that the word of the LORD in your mouth is truth."
verses.18:1: Now it happened after many days that the word of the LORD came to Elijah in the third year, saying, "Go, present yourself to Ahab, and I will give rain on the face of the ground."
verses.18:2: So Elijah went to present himself to Ahab. Now the famine was severe in Samaria.
verses.18:3: And Ahab called for Obadiah, who was over the household. Now Obadiah feared the LORD greatly.
verses.18:4: For when Jezebel was cutting off the prophets of the LORD, Obadiah took a hundred prophets and hid them, fifty men to a cave, and sustained them with bread and water.
verses.18:5: Then Ahab said to Obadiah, "Go through the land to all the springs of water and to all the wadis; perhaps we will find grass and keep horses and mules alive, and not cut off any of the livestock."
verses.18:6: So they divided the land between themselves to pass through it: Ahab went in one direction by himself, and Obadiah went in another direction by himself.
verses.18:7: Now as Obadiah was on the way, look, Elijah came to meet him. And he recognized him, fell on his face, and said, "Is this really you, my lord Elijah?"
verses.18:8: And he said to him, "It is I. Go, tell your lord, 'Here is Elijah.'"
verses.18:9: And he said, "What sin have I committed, that you are giving your servant into the hand of Ahab to put me to death?
verses.18:10: As the LORD your God lives, there is not a nation or kingdom where my lord has not sent to search for you; and when they said, 'He is not here,' he put the kingdom and the nation under oath that they could not find you.
verses.18:11: And now you are saying, 'Go, tell your lord, "Here is Elijah."'
verses.18:12: And it will happen that as soon as I leave you, the Spirit of the LORD will carry you away to where I do not know; so when I come to tell Ahab and he cannot find you, he will kill me, although your servant has feared the LORD from my youth.
verses.18:13: Has it not been told to my lord what I did when Jezebel killed the prophets of the LORD, how I hid a hundred men of the prophets of the LORD, fifty men each in a cave, and sustained them with bread and water?
verses.18:14: And now you are saying, 'Go, tell your lord, "Here is Elijah"'; and he will kill me."
verses.18:15: Then Elijah said, "As the LORD of hosts lives, before whom I stand, I will surely present myself to him today."
verses.18:16: So Obadiah went to meet Ahab and told him; and Ahab went to meet Elijah.
verses.18:17: And it happened when Ahab saw Elijah that Ahab said to him, "Is this really you, troubler of Israel?"
verses.18:18: He said, "I have not troubled Israel; rather, you and your father's house have, because you have forsaken the commandments of the LORD and you have gone after the Baals.
verses.18:19: So now send and gather all Israel to me at Mount Carmel, along with the four hundred and fifty prophets of Baal and the four hundred prophets of Asherah, who eat at Jezebel's table."
verses.18:20: So Ahab sent throughout all the sons of Israel and gathered the prophets together at Mount Carmel.
verses.18:21: Then Elijah drew near to all the people and said, "How long will you keep limping between two divided opinions? If the LORD is God, go after Him; but if Baal, go after him." Yet the people did not answer him a word.
verses.18:22: Then Elijah said to the people, "I alone remain as a prophet of the LORD, while Baal's prophets are four hundred and fifty men.
verses.18:23: Now let them give us two bulls, and let them choose one bull for themselves, cut it into pieces, and lay it on the wood, yet set no fire; and I will prepare the other bull and lay it on the wood, and I will set no fire.
verses.18:24: Then you will call on the name of your god, and I will call on the name of the LORD; and the God who answers by fire, He is God." And all the people answered and said, "The word is good."
verses.18:25: Then Elijah said to the prophets of Baal, "Choose one bull for yourselves and prepare it first, since you are the many, and call on the name of your god, yet set no fire."
verses.18:26: So they took the bull that was given to them and prepared it, and they called on the name of Baal from morning until noon, saying, "Baal, answer us!" Yet there was no voice and no one answering. And they limped around the altar that had been made.
verses.18:27: Then it happened at noon that Elijah mocked them and said, "Call out in a loud voice, since he is a god! Maybe he is deep in thought, or he has stepped aside, or he is on a journey; perhaps he is asleep and must wake up."
verses.18:28: So they called out in a loud voice and gashed themselves according to their custom with swords and lances, until blood poured out over them.
verses.18:29: And when noon passed, they raved until the time of presenting the grain offering; yet there was no voice, no one answering, and no one paying attention.
verses.18:30: Then Elijah said to all the people, "Come near to me." So all the people came near to him. And he repaired the altar of the LORD that had been torn down.
verses.18:31: And Elijah took twelve stones, according to the number of the tribes of the sons of Jacob, to whom the word of the LORD had come, saying, "Israel will be your name."
verses.18:32: With the stones he built an altar in the name of the LORD, and around the altar he made a trench with the capacity of about two seahs of seed.
verses.18:33: Then he arranged the wood, cut the bull into pieces, and laid it on the wood.
verses.18:34: He said, "Fill four jars with water and pour it onto the burnt offering and onto the wood." Then he said, "Do it a second time," and they did it a second time. He said, "Do it a third time," and they did it a third time.
verses.18:35: And the water flowed around the altar, and he also filled the trench with water.
verses.18:36: And it happened at the time of presenting the grain offering that Elijah the prophet drew near and said, "LORD, God of Abraham, Isaac, and Israel, let it be known today that You are God in Israel, and that I am Your servant, and that at Your word I have done all these things.
verses.18:37: Answer me, LORD, answer me, so that this people may know that You, LORD, are God, and that You Yourself have turned their heart back."
verses.18:38: Then the fire of the LORD fell and consumed the burnt offering, the wood, the stones, and the dust, and it licked up the water that was in the trench.
verses.18:39: And all the people saw this, fell on their faces, and said, "The LORD, He is God! The LORD, He is God!"
verses.18:40: Then Elijah said to them, "Seize the prophets of Baal; let not one man among them escape." So they seized them, and Elijah brought them down to the Wadi Kishon and slaughtered them there.
verses.18:41: Then Elijah said to Ahab, "Go up, eat and drink, for there is the sound of the roar of rain."
verses.18:42: So Ahab went up to eat and drink, while Elijah went up to the summit of Carmel; and he crouched down to the ground and placed his face between his knees.
verses.18:43: He said to his servant, "Please go up and look toward the sea." So he went up, looked, and said, "There is nothing." And he said, "Go back seven times."
verses.18:44: And it happened on the seventh time that he said, "Look, a small cloud like a man's palm is rising from the sea." Then he said, "Go up, tell Ahab, 'Harness up and go down, so that the rain does not detain you.'"
verses.18:45: In a little while the sky grew dark with clouds and wind, and there was a heavy rain. And Ahab rode off and went to Jezreel.
verses.18:46: Then the hand of the LORD came upon Elijah, and he girded up his waist and ran ahead of Ahab all the way to the entrance of Jezreel.
verses.19:1: Ahab reported to Jezebel everything that Elijah had done, and all about how he had killed all the prophets with the sword.
verses.19:2: So Jezebel sent a messenger to Elijah, saying, "May the gods do so and add still more; surely about this time tomorrow I will make your life like the life of one of them."
verses.19:3: When he saw this, he rose and went for his life, came to Beersheba, which belongs to Judah, and left his attendant there.
verses.19:4: He himself walked a day's journey into the wilderness, and came and sat beneath a single broom bush. He asked for himself to die, and said, "Enough! Now, LORD, take my life, because I am no better than my fathers."
verses.19:5: He lay down and fell asleep beneath a single broom bush. And look, an angel was touching him, and said to him, "Get up, eat."
verses.19:6: He looked, and there at his head was a bread cake baked on hot stones and a jug of water. So he ate and drank, and lay down again.
verses.19:7: The angel of the LORD returned a second time and touched him, and said, "Get up, eat, because the journey is too much for you."
verses.19:8: So he got up, ate, and drank, and walked in the strength of that meal for forty days and forty nights as far as the mountain of God, Horeb.
verses.19:9: There he came into the cave and spent the night there. And look, the word of the LORD came to him, and He said to him, "What are you doing here, Elijah?"
verses.19:10: He said, "I have been deeply zealous for the LORD, God of hosts, because the sons of Israel have abandoned Your covenant, demolished Your altars, and killed Your prophets with the sword. I myself alone remain, and they are seeking my life to take it."
verses.19:11: And He said, "Go out and stand on the mountain before the LORD." And look, the LORD was passing by, and a great and powerful wind was tearing mountains apart and shattering rocks before the LORD; the LORD was not in the wind. And after the wind, an earthquake; the LORD was not in the earthquake.
verses.19:12: And after the earthquake, a fire; the LORD was not in the fire. And after the fire, a sound of delicate silence.
verses.19:13: When Elijah heard this, he covered his face with his cloak, went out, and stood at the opening of the cave. And look, a voice came to him and said, "What are you doing here, Elijah?"
verses.19:14: He said, "I have been deeply zealous for the LORD, God of hosts, because the sons of Israel have abandoned Your covenant, demolished Your altars, and killed Your prophets with the sword. I myself alone remain, and they are seeking my life to take it."
verses.19:15: Then the LORD said to him, "Go, return along your way to the wilderness of Damascus; when you arrive, anoint Hazael as king over Aram.
verses.19:16: You shall also anoint Jehu son of Nimshi as king over Israel, and you shall anoint Elisha son of Shaphat, from Abel-meholah, as prophet in place of you.
verses.19:17: And it will happen that whoever escapes from Hazael's sword, Jehu will put to death, and whoever escapes from Jehu's sword, Elisha will put to death.
verses.19:18: Yet I will leave seven thousand remaining in Israel: all the knees that have not knelt to Baal, and every mouth that has not kissed him."
verses.19:19: So he departed from there and found Elisha son of Shaphat while he was plowing; twelve yokes of oxen were ahead of him, and he himself was with the twelfth. Elijah crossed over to him and cast his cloak onto him.
verses.19:20: He left the oxen, ran after Elijah, and said, "Please let me kiss my father and my mother, and then I will go after you." And he said to him, "Go, return, for what have I done to you?"
verses.19:21: So he turned back from following him, took the yoke of oxen and slaughtered them, boiled their meat with the gear of the oxen, and gave it to the people, and they ate. Then he got up, went after Elijah, and served him.
verses.20:1: It happened after these things that there was a vineyard belonging to Naboth the Jezreelite, which was in Jezreel, next to the palace of Ahab, king of Samaria.
verses.20:2: Ahab spoke to Naboth, saying, "Give me your vineyard so that it may be a vegetable garden for me, because it is close next to my house, and I will give you a better vineyard than it in its place. If it is good in your eyes, I will give you silver as the price of this one."
verses.20:3: Naboth said to Ahab, "Far be it from me before the LORD to give the inheritance of my fathers to you."
verses.20:4: So Ahab went to his house, sullen and indignant over the word that Naboth the Jezreelite had spoken to him, for he had said, "I will not give you the inheritance of my fathers." He lay down on his bed, turned his face away, and ate no food.
verses.20:5: Then his wife Jezebel came to him and spoke to him, "Why is it that your spirit is sullen, and you are not eating food?"
verses.20:6: He spoke to her, "Because I spoke to Naboth the Jezreelite and said to him, 'Give me your vineyard for silver, or if you wish, I will give you a vineyard in its place.' Yet he said, 'I will not give you my vineyard.'"
verses.20:7: His wife Jezebel said to him, "Do you now exercise kingship over Israel? Get up, eat food, and let your heart be glad; I myself will give you the vineyard of Naboth the Jezreelite."
verses.20:8: So she wrote letters in the name of Ahab, sealed them with his seal, and sent letters to the elders and to the nobles who were in his city, those living with Naboth.
verses.20:9: She wrote in the letters, saying, "Call a fast, and seat Naboth at the head of the people.
verses.20:10: And seat two men, sons of worthlessness, opposite him, and let them testify against him, saying, 'You have cursed God and the king.' Then bring him out and stone him so that he dies."
verses.20:11: So the men of his city—the elders and the nobles residing in his city—carried out what Jezebel had sent to them, according to what was written in the letters that she had sent to them.
verses.20:12: They called a fast and seated Naboth at the head of the people.
verses.20:13: Then the two men, sons of worthlessness, came in and sat opposite him; and the men of worthlessness testified against Naboth before the people, saying, "Naboth has cursed God and the king." So they brought him outside the city and stoned him with stones, and he died.
verses.20:14: Then they sent word to Jezebel, saying, "Naboth has been stoned and has died."
verses.20:15: When Jezebel heard that Naboth had been stoned and had died, Jezebel said to Ahab, "Get up, take possession of the vineyard of Naboth the Jezreelite, which he refused to give you for silver, because Naboth is not alive—he is dead."
verses.20:16: When Ahab heard that Naboth had died, Ahab got up to go down to the vineyard of Naboth the Jezreelite to take possession of it.
verses.20:17: Then the word of the LORD came to Elijah the Tishbite, saying,
verses.20:18: "Get up, go down to meet Ahab, king of Israel, who is in Samaria. Look, he is in the vineyard of Naboth, where he has gone down to take possession of it.
verses.20:19: And you shall speak to him, saying, 'This is what the LORD says: Have you murdered and also taken possession?' And you shall speak to him, saying, 'This is what the LORD says: In the place where the dogs licked Naboth's blood, the dogs will lick your blood, even yours.'"
verses.20:20: Ahab said to Elijah, "Have you found me, my enemy?" He answered, "I have found you, because you have sold yourself to do what is evil in the eyes of the LORD.
verses.20:21: Look, I am bringing calamity upon you; I will sweep clean after you, and I will cut off from Ahab every male, both confined and free in Israel.
verses.20:22: I will make your house like the house of Jeroboam son of Nebat and like the house of Baasha son of Ahijah, because of the provocation by which you have provoked anger and caused Israel to sin.
verses.20:23: And concerning Jezebel also, the LORD has spoken, saying, 'The dogs will eat Jezebel by the rampart of Jezreel.'
verses.20:24: Whoever belonging to Ahab dies in the city, the dogs will eat; and whoever dies in the field, the birds of the sky will eat."
verses.20:25: Indeed, there was no one like Ahab, who sold himself to do what is evil in the eyes of the LORD, whom his wife Jezebel incited.
verses.20:26: He behaved most detestably in going after idols, according to everything that the Amorites had done, whom the LORD had dispossessed from before the sons of Israel.
verses.20:27: When Ahab heard these words, he tore his garments, put sackcloth on his flesh, and fasted; he lay in sackcloth and walked about softly.
verses.20:28: Then the word of the LORD came to Elijah the Tishbite, saying,
verses.20:29: "Have you seen that Ahab has humbled himself before Me? Since he has humbled himself before Me, I will not bring the calamity during his days; in the days of his son I will bring the calamity upon his house."
verses.21:1: Now Ben-hadad, king of Aram, assembled his entire army, and thirty-two kings were with him, as well as horses and chariots. He went up, laid siege to Samaria, and fought against it.
verses.21:2: He sent messengers into the city to Ahab, king of Israel.
verses.21:3: And he said to him, "This is what Ben-hadad says: 'Your silver and your gold belong to me, and the finest of your wives and your sons belong to me.'"
verses.21:4: The king of Israel answered and said, "According to your word, my lord the king: I belong to you, together with everything that is mine."
verses.21:5: The messengers returned and said, "This is what Ben-hadad says: 'Indeed, I sent to you, saying, "You must give to me your silver and your gold, your wives and your sons,"
verses.21:6: nevertheless, about this time tomorrow I will send my servants to you, and they will search through your house and the houses of your servants; and everything precious to your eyes they will put in their hands and take away.'"
verses.21:7: Then the king of Israel summoned all the elders of the land and said, "Please take note and see how this man is seeking harm; for he sent to me for my wives and my sons, and for my silver and my gold, and I did not hold them back from him."
verses.21:8: All the elders and all the people said to him, "Do not listen, and do not agree."
verses.21:9: So he said to the messengers of Ben-hadad, "Tell my lord the king, 'Everything for which you sent to your servant at first I will do, but this matter I cannot do.'" The messengers went off and brought back word to him.
verses.21:10: Then Ben-hadad sent to him and said, "May the gods deal thus with me, and add still more, if the dust of Samaria proves enough for handfuls for all the people who follow at my feet."
verses.21:11: The king of Israel answered and said, "Tell him, 'The one who buckles on his armor should not boast like the one who unbuckles it.'"
verses.21:12: When he heard this word, while he was drinking, he and the kings in the shelters, he said to his servants, "Position yourselves!" And they positioned themselves against the city.
verses.21:13: Now a certain prophet drew near to Ahab, king of Israel, and said, "This is what the LORD says: 'Have you seen this entire great multitude? Look, I am giving it into your hand today, and you will know that I am the LORD.'"
verses.21:14: Ahab asked, "By whom?" He said, "This is what the LORD says: 'By the young men of the officials of the provinces.'" Then he asked, "Who will open the battle?" And he said, "You."
verses.21:15: Then he mustered the young men of the officials of the provinces, and there were two hundred thirty-two; and after them he mustered all the people, all the sons of Israel, seven thousand.
verses.21:16: They went out at midday, while Ben-hadad was drinking to drunkenness in the shelters, he and the kings, the thirty-two kings who were aiding him.
verses.21:17: The young men of the officials of the provinces went out first. Ben-hadad sent out, and they reported to him, saying, "Men have come out from Samaria."
verses.21:18: He said, "If they have come out for peace, capture them alive; and if they have come out for war, capture them alive."
verses.21:19: So these went out from the city: the young men of the officials of the provinces, and the army that was behind them.
verses.21:20: They struck down each one his man, and the Arameans fled as Israel pursued them; and Ben-hadad, king of Aram, escaped on a horse along with horsemen.
verses.21:21: Then the king of Israel went out and struck down the horses and the chariots, and inflicted a great blow on the Arameans.
verses.21:22: Then the prophet drew near to the king of Israel and said to him, "Go, strengthen yourself, and know and see what you should do; for at the return of the year the king of Aram is coming up against you."
verses.21:23: Now the servants of the king of Aram said to him, "Their God is a God of the mountains; for that reason they were stronger than we were. However, let us fight with them on the plain, and certainly we will be stronger than they are.
verses.21:24: And do this thing: remove the kings, each one from his position, and set governors in their place.
verses.21:25: And as for you, number for yourself an army like the army that fell from you, horse for horse and chariot for chariot; then let us fight with them on the plain, and certainly we will be stronger than they are." So he listened to their voice and did so.
verses.21:26: At the return of the year, Ben-hadad mustered the Arameans and marched up to Aphek for battle with Israel.
verses.21:27: The sons of Israel were also mustered and provisioned, and they went to meet them; the sons of Israel encamped opposite them like two small flocks of goats, while the Arameans filled the land.
verses.21:28: Then the man of God drew near, spoke to the king of Israel, and said, "This is what the LORD says: 'Because the Arameans have said, "The LORD is a God of the mountains, and He is not a God of the valleys," I will give this entire great multitude into your hand, and you will know that I am the LORD.'"
verses.21:29: They encamped facing one another for seven days. On the seventh day the battle commenced, and the sons of Israel struck down the Arameans, one hundred thousand foot soldiers in a single day.
verses.21:30: Those who remained fled to Aphek, into the city, and the wall fell on twenty-seven thousand of the remaining men. Ben-hadad also fled and went into the city, into a chamber within a chamber.
verses.21:31: His servants said to him, "Look now, we have heard that the kings of the house of Israel are kings of loyal love. Please let us put sackcloth around our waists and ropes on our heads, and go out to the king of Israel; perhaps he will preserve your life."
verses.21:32: So they bound sackcloth around their waists, with ropes on their heads, came to the king of Israel, and said, "Your servant Ben-hadad says, 'Please let me keep my life.'" And he said, "Is he still alive? He is my brother."
verses.21:33: Now the men were watching for an omen, and they hurried to confirm whether it came from him, and said, "Your brother Ben-hadad!" He said, "Go, bring him." Then Ben-hadad came out to him, and he brought him up onto the chariot.
verses.21:34: He said to him, "The cities that my father took from your father I will return, and you may establish streets for yourself in Damascus, just as my father established in Samaria." "And as for me, under this covenant I will release you." So he made a covenant with him and released him.
verses.21:35: Now one man from the sons of the prophets said to his companion by the word of the LORD, "Please strike me." The man, however, refused to strike him.
verses.21:36: Then he said to him, "Because you have not heeded the voice of the LORD, look: as you go away from me, a lion will strike you down." And he departed from beside him, and a lion found him and struck him down.
verses.21:37: Then he found another man and said, "Please strike me." So the man struck him hard, wounding him.
verses.21:38: Then the prophet went and stood waiting for the king along the road, and disguised himself with a bandage across his eyes.
verses.21:39: While the king was passing by, he cried out to the king and said, "Your servant went out into the midst of the battle; and look, a man turned aside and brought a man to me, and said, 'Guard this man. If he turns up missing at all, then your life will be in place of his life, or you will weigh out a talent of silver.'
verses.21:40: Yet while your servant was occupied here and there, he was no longer there." The king of Israel said to him, "That is your verdict; you yourself have determined it."
verses.21:41: Then he hurried and removed the bandage from over his eyes, and the king of Israel recognized him, that he was one of the prophets.
verses.21:42: He said to him, "This is what the LORD says: 'Because you have released from your hand the man devoted by Me to destruction, your life will be in place of his life, and your people in place of his people.'"
verses.21:43: So the king of Israel went to his house, resentful and angry, and came to Samaria.
verses.22:1: They remained for three years; there was no war between Aram and Israel.
verses.22:2: Now it happened in the third year that Jehoshaphat king of Judah went down to the king of Israel.
verses.22:3: The king of Israel said to his servants, "Do you know that Ramoth-Gilead is ours, yet we remain quiet rather than taking it from the hand of the king of Aram?"
verses.22:4: Then he said to Jehoshaphat, "Will you go with me to war at Ramoth-Gilead?" And Jehoshaphat said to the king of Israel, "I am like you, my people are like your people, my horses are like your horses."
verses.22:5: And Jehoshaphat said to the king of Israel, "First, please inquire for the word of the LORD."
verses.22:6: So the king of Israel assembled the prophets, around four hundred men, and asked them, "Should I go against Ramoth-Gilead to war, or should I hold back?" They replied, "Go up, and the Lord will give it into the king's hand."
verses.22:7: But Jehoshaphat asked, "Is there not still a prophet of the LORD here, so that we may inquire from him?"
verses.22:8: The king of Israel answered Jehoshaphat, "There is still one man from whom to inquire of the LORD, yet I hate him, because he does not prophesy good about me, only evil—Micaiah son of Imlah." Jehoshaphat said, "Let the king not say that."
verses.22:9: So the king of Israel summoned a court official and said, "Bring Micaiah son of Imlah quickly."
verses.22:10: Now the king of Israel and Jehoshaphat king of Judah were each seated on his throne, clothed in robes, at a threshing floor at the entrance of Samaria's gate, while all the prophets were prophesying in front of them.
verses.22:11: Zedekiah son of Chenaanah made iron horns for himself and said, "This is what the LORD says: 'With these you will gore Aram until you destroy them completely.'"
verses.22:12: And all the prophets were prophesying in the same way, saying, "Go up to Ramoth-Gilead and succeed, and the LORD will give it into the king's hand."
verses.22:13: Now the messenger who went to call Micaiah spoke to him, saying, "Look now, the words of the prophets are, with one mouth, good toward the king. Let your word, please, be like the word of one of them, and speak what is good."
verses.22:14: Micaiah answered, "As the LORD lives, whatever the LORD says to me, that is what I will speak."
verses.22:15: When he came to the king, the king said to him, "Micaiah, should we go to Ramoth-Gilead to war, or should we hold back?" And he said to him, "Go up and succeed, and the LORD will give it into the king's hand."
verses.22:16: But the king said to him, "How many times must I put you under oath that you will speak to me nothing except truth in the name of the LORD?"
verses.22:17: So he said, "I saw all Israel scattered across the mountains, like sheep with no shepherd. And the LORD said, 'There is no master for these; let each man return to his house in peace.'"
verses.22:18: Then the king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat, "Did I not say to you, 'He does not prophesy good about me, only evil'?"
verses.22:19: And he said, "Therefore, listen to the word of the LORD: I saw the LORD seated on His throne, with the whole host of heaven standing beside Him at His right hand and at His left.
verses.22:20: And the LORD asked, 'Who will entice Ahab so that he will go up and fall at Ramoth-Gilead?' One said one thing, while another was saying something else.
verses.22:21: Then the spirit came out, stood before the LORD, and said, 'I will entice him.' And the LORD said to him, 'By what means?'
verses.22:22: And he said, 'I will go out and become a spirit of falsehood in the mouth of all his prophets.' Then He said, 'You will entice him and also prevail. Go out and do so.'
verses.22:23: And now, look, the LORD has placed a spirit of falsehood in the mouth of all these prophets of yours, and the LORD has spoken disaster against you."
verses.22:24: Then Zedekiah son of Chenaanah stepped up, struck Micaiah on the cheek, and asked, "Which way did the Spirit of the LORD pass from me to speak with you?"
verses.22:25: Micaiah replied, "Look, you will see on that day when you go into a room within a room to hide yourself."
verses.22:26: Then the king of Israel said, "Take Micaiah and return him to Amon, commander of the city, and to Joash, the king's son,
verses.22:27: and say, 'This is what the king says: Put this man in prison and feed him bread of distress and water of distress until I come back in peace.'"
verses.22:28: But Micaiah said, "If you really return in peace, then the LORD has not spoken through me." And he also said, "Listen, all you peoples!"
verses.22:29: Then the king of Israel and Jehoshaphat king of Judah went up to Ramoth-Gilead.
verses.22:30: The king of Israel told Jehoshaphat, "I will disguise myself and enter the battle, while you put on your robes." So the king of Israel disguised himself and entered the battle.
verses.22:31: Now the king of Aram had ordered his thirty-two chariot commanders, saying, "Do not fight with small or great, except with the king of Israel alone."
verses.22:32: Now when the chariot commanders saw Jehoshaphat, they said, "Indeed, this is the king of Israel!" And they turned aside against him to fight, so Jehoshaphat cried out.
verses.22:33: When the chariot commanders saw that he was not the king of Israel, they turned back from following after him.
verses.22:34: But a man drew a bow at random and struck the king of Israel between the joints and the breastplate. So he said to his chariot driver, "Turn your hand and bring me out of the army, because I have been wounded."
verses.22:35: The battle grew fierce on that day, and the king was kept standing in the chariot facing Aram; he died in the evening, and the blood of the wound poured into the hollow of the chariot.
verses.22:36: Then the shout went through the army as the sun went down, saying, "Each man to his city, and each man to his land!"
verses.22:37: Thus the king died and was brought into Samaria, and they buried the king in Samaria.
verses.22:38: And the chariot was rinsed at the pool of Samaria, and the dogs licked up his blood, while the prostitutes bathed, according to the word of the LORD that He had spoken.
verses.22:39: Now the rest of the deeds of Ahab, and everything that he did, and the house of ivory that he built, and all the cities that he built, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel?
verses.22:40: So Ahab lay down with his fathers, and his son Ahaziah reigned in his place.
verses.22:41: And Jehoshaphat son of Asa began to reign over Judah in the fourth year of Ahab, king of Israel.
verses.22:42: Jehoshaphat was thirty-five years old when he became king, and for twenty-five years he reigned in Jerusalem. The name of his mother was Azubah daughter of Shilhi.
verses.22:43: And he walked in the entire way of his father Asa; he did not turn aside from it, doing what was right in the eyes of the LORD.
verses.22:44: However, the high places were not removed; the people were still sacrificing and burning incense at the high places.
verses.22:45: And Jehoshaphat made peace with the king of Israel.
verses.22:46: Now the rest of the deeds of Jehoshaphat, and his might that he demonstrated, and how he fought, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah?
verses.22:51: Then Jehoshaphat lay down with his fathers and was buried with his fathers in the city of his father David, and his son Jehoram reigned in his place.
verses.22:52: Ahaziah son of Ahab became king over Israel in Samaria in the seventeenth year of Jehoshaphat, king of Judah, and he reigned over Israel for two years.
verses.22:53: He did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD; he walked in the way of his father, and in the way of his mother, and in the way of Jeroboam son of Nebat, who made Israel sin.
verses.22:54: He served Baal and bowed down to him, and he provoked the LORD, the God of Israel, to anger, in accordance with everything that his father had done.

notes.1:6: Literally "and she bore him after Absalom," using a Qal perfect 3fs verb without an explicit subject in this verse, either referring back to Haggith in v. 5 or serving as an idiomatic impersonal construction for "he was born."
notes.1:18: The Masoretic Text reads "and now" a second time here rather than "and you," the reading of some Hebrew manuscripts and ancient versions that differs by a single consonant.
notes.1:27: Following the Masoretic Qere (singular, "your servant"); the written Ketiv reads the plural ("your servants").
notes.1:37: Following the Masoretic Qere, which reads the full Qal imperfect form (used optatively in non-initial position after "so," parallel to the following volitive verb); the written Ketiv has the short Qal jussive form ("may He be").
notes.1:47: Following the Masoretic Qere ("God"); the written Ketiv reads "your God."
notes.2:22: The Hebrew ends elliptically with "for him, and for Abiathar the priest, and for Joab son of Zeruiah" (resuming "ask for him"), implying that Abiathar and Joab stood behind Adonijah's bid for the throne.
notes.2:23: Following the self-imprecatory oath formula ("Thus may God do to me, and so may He add"), Hebrew ki introduces an emphatic sworn assertion ("surely"), and the preposition be- with "his own life" functions as a beth of price ("at the cost of his own life").
notes.2:24: Ketiv/Qere: the qere reads the standard Hiphil wayyiqtol with 1cs suffix "and seated me" (wayyoshivani), whereas the ketiv displays an orthographic variant (wywshybyny) with the same meaning.
notes.2:35: The last two sentences are Masoretic 9:23 (the 550 chief officers over the work) and 9:25 (Solomon's offerings three times a year), carried in this verse following the Saints (Greek) verse arrangement. In the final sentence, the Hiphil infinitive absolute "burn incense" continues the preceding frequentative verb, and "with it, which was before the LORD" is a compressed Hebrew reference to burning incense at the altar before the LORD.
notes.2:46: From "Judah and Israel were numerous" onward, this verse carries the Masoretic summary verses 4:20, 5:1, and 5:5 (traditional English 4:20-21, 25), following the Saints (Greek) verse arrangement.
notes.3:4: The verb ya'aleh ("would offer up") is a Hiphil imperfect of alah, cognate with olot ("burnt offerings"), expressing either customary practice at Gibeon or prolonged action on that occasion.
notes.3:9: Literally "a listening heart" (lev shomea, Qal active participle of shama), denoting a heart attentive to God and discerning in judicial hearings (compare "to hear justice" in 3:11). The adjective kaved ("weighty") conveys both the vastness of the nation and the heavy burden of judging it.
notes.3:10: Here and in 3:15 the Masoretic Hebrew reads Adonai ("the Lord") rather than the divine name ("the LORD").
notes.3:13: The Hebrew uses the Qal perfect verb hayah ("was" or "has been") with the forward-looking phrase "all your days," conveying the assured outcome of God's promise ("will be").
notes.3:26: The idiom nikhmeru rachameha (Niphal perfect of kamar with rachamim) literally means "her compassion grew warm," expressing intense maternal yearning. Here and in 3:27 the Hebrew shifts from yeled ("child" in 3:25) to the Qal passive participle yalud ("born one" or "newborn").
notes.4:5: Hebrew kohen usually means "priest," though some take it here as a royal administrative title; re'eh ha-melekh ("the king's friend") is a technical court title for a trusted royal adviser.
notes.4:7: Following the Masoretic qere ha'echad ("each one," with the distributive definite article); the written ketiv echad omits the article ("one"). Both occurrences of "provide" translate the Pilpel stem of kul ("sustain" or "supply provisions").
notes.4:16: Hebrew u-ve'alot can be parsed either as "and in Aloth" (repeating the preposition be-, as in 4:9) or as "and Bealoth" (taking the initial letter as part of the place name).
notes.4:18: Hebrew netsiv echad asher ba'arets ("one governor who was in the land") is elliptical, either stressing that a single governor oversaw this vast Transjordanian region or referring to one governor appointed in Judah.
notes.5:1: This verse translates Masoretic 5:7-8 (traditional English 4:27-28), following the Saints (Greek) verse arrangement; Masoretic 5:1 and 5:5 are carried in 2:46, and 5:6 in 10:26.
notes.5:14: The first sentence is Masoretic 3:1 and the last sentence is Masoretic 9:16 (Pharaoh's capture of Gezer), carried in this verse following the Saints (Greek) verse arrangement.
notes.5:17: The qere reads raglay ('my feet'), whereas the ketiv reads rglo ('his foot' or 'his feet', referring to David). Although 'warfare' (hammilchamah) is singular, the following verb ('surrounded him') and object pronoun ('them') are plural ad sensum, referring to the hostile forces.
notes.5:23: The noun doberot ('rafts') is a hapax legomenon in the Hebrew Bible; the Piel verb nippastim ('break them apart') describes dismantling the lashed timber rafts upon arrival.
notes.5:24: Here and in 5:32 the Hebrew text spells the Tyrian king's name Hirom, an alternate vocalization of Hiram.
notes.6:1: The last two sentences ("In the fourth year the foundation... over seven years") are Masoretic 6:37-38, carried in this verse following the Saints (Greek) verse arrangement.
notes.6:4: The architectural phrase challone shequfim atumim ('framed, recessed windows') uses two rare terms of uncertain design, likely denoting fixed windows set within beveled or recessed frames.
notes.6:5: Here and in 6:6 and 6:10, the qere reads yatsia ('side structure' or 'story'), distinguishing the architectural term from the ketiv yatsua (elsewhere 'bed' or 'couch').
notes.6:8: The Hebrew text explicitly reads hattikhonah ('the middle') for the entrance chamber, even though stairs ascend from it to 'the middle' story; lulim ('winding stairs') is a hapax legomenon whose exact construction is uncertain.
notes.6:20: Hebrew lifne haddevir literally means 'in front of the inner sanctuary,' though the cubical dimensions refer to the interior of the inner sanctuary itself. The final clause ('he overlaid an altar with cedar') may alternatively mean 'he overlaid the cedar altar' (with gold, cf. 6:22).
notes.6:31: The architectural expressions chamishit ('a fifth part') here and me'et revi'it ('of a fourth part') in 6:33 are obscure; they are variously understood as one-fifth and one-fourth of the wall's width or as five-sided and four-sided doorway frames.
notes.7:6: The Masoretic Hebrew reads 'the pillars' and 'on top of the pomegranates,' a well-known textual transposition of the two nouns (compare 7:27-28). At 'the latticework,' the qere adds the definite article omitted in the ketiv.
notes.7:10: For 'and a line,' the qere reads the standard spelling veqav, whereas the ketiv writes the longer orthographic form veqaveh with the same meaning.
notes.7:22: At 'and on its panels,' the qere omits a redundant conjunction vav present in the ketiv. The difficult phrase translated 'according to the open space on each' literally refers to the bare or clear space available on each section.
notes.7:31: For 'these,' the qere reads ha'elleh ('all these articles'), whereas the ketiv reads ha'ohel ('all the articles of the tent').
notes.7:44: The Masoretic Hebrew literally reads 'from the floor to the floor,' likely referring to the full vertical span from the lower floor to the upper floor or ceiling level.
notes.8:9: Elliptical Hebrew: MT literally reads "where the LORD cut with the sons of Israel," omitting the usual object berit ("covenant") after the Qal verb karat ("cut, make [a covenant]").
notes.8:26: Ketiv/Qere: the written ketiv is plural ("Your words"), while the read qere translated here is singular ("Your word"), agreeing with the singular Niphal verb ye'amen ("prove true").
notes.8:30: MT uses the directional preposition 'el ("to") before both "the place of Your dwelling" and "heaven," either functioning locatively ("in") or depicting prayers ascending to God's heavenly dwelling place.
notes.8:31: MT opens the conditional clause with 'et 'asher ("if/when") and spells the Qal verb "laid" with shin (nasha') rather than sin (nasa'). The phrase uba' 'alah is terse, literally either "and he comes [and] swears [an oath]" or "and an oath comes."
notes.8:35: The verb ta'anem ("You humble them") is parsed as Hiphil of 'anah II ("afflict, humble"), fitting the drought context; the form is homographic with the Qal of 'anah I ("answer").
notes.8:48: Ketiv/Qere: the written ketiv omits the final yod (bnyt), while the pointed qere translated here is first-person singular baniti ("I have built"), matching 8:43 and 8:44.
notes.8:59: The Hebrew idiom debar-yom beyomo (literally "the matter of a day in its day") denotes each day's ongoing need or requirement.
notes.9:8: The Masoretic Hebrew reads "will be exalted" (yihyeh elyon), understood concessively here ("exalted though it may be"; compare 2 Chronicles 7:21). Some ancient versions read "a heap of ruins."
notes.9:9: The final sentence ("Once Pharaoh's daughter... the Millo") is Masoretic 9:24, carried here following the Saints (Greek) verse arrangement. The qere reads the plural "and bowed down," while the ketiv has a singular or defective spelling.
notes.9:11: The Piel verb nissa here means "supplied" or "assisted" with gifts (rather than "lifted up"). After the adverb az ("then"), the imperfect verb yitten has past narrative force ("then ... gave").
notes.10:5: The Masoretic vocalization olato ("his burnt offering") with the verb yaaleh ("offered up") is followed here; the parallel in 2 Chronicles 9:4 reads "his ascent" (stairway), which some interpreters read here as well.
notes.10:12: The Hebrew noun translated "supports" (misad) occurs only here in the Hebrew Bible; derived from the verb meaning "to support," it may denote structural supports, railings, or pillars (compare "steps" in 2 Chronicles 9:11).
notes.10:15: The Masoretic Hebrew vocalizes ha-erev ("the mixed peoples"; compare Jeremiah 25:24), whereas the parallel in 2 Chronicles 9:14 reads ha-arav ("Arabia").
notes.10:22: The verse up to "his chariots and his horsemen" is Masoretic 9:15 and 9:17-22 (Solomon's forced labor and building works), carried here following the Saints (Greek) verse arrangement; the final sentence is Masoretic 10:22. For the desert city, the qere reads "Tadmor" (compare 2 Chronicles 8:4) while the ketiv reads "Tamar" (compare Ezekiel 47:19). The final exotic import translated "peacocks" (tukkiyyim) is traditionally so rendered, though some scholars understand it as "baboons" or a species of monkey.
notes.10:26: The first sentence is Masoretic 5:6 (traditional English 4:26), carried here following the Saints (Greek) verse arrangement.
notes.10:28: The Hebrew miqweh is read here as the preposition "from" prefixed to the region Kue (ancient Cilicia, renowned for horse breeding), though older traditions took it as a common noun meaning "a drove" or "linen yarn."
notes.11:11: The Hebrew idiom literally reads "this has been with you," expressing a settled course of conduct or mindset harbored by Solomon.
notes.11:14: The sentences about Rezon son of Eliada are Masoretic 11:23-24, carried in this verse following the Saints (Greek) verse arrangement.
notes.11:25: The clause "along with the harm that Hadad did" translates an elliptical Hebrew construction (lit. "and with the evil which Hadad") where the verb is left implied.
notes.11:33: The Hebrew text uses third-person plural verbs ("they have forsaken Me ... bowed down ... have not walked") before concluding with the singular phrase "David his father," broadening Solomon's apostasy to implicate the nation as a whole.
notes.12:3: Ketiv reads plural "they came" while the translated Qere reads singular "he came," agreeing grammatically with the first element of the compound subject; the same Ketiv/Qere occurs in 12:21.
notes.12:7: Ketiv reads singular "and he spoke," while the translated Qere reads plural "and they spoke," agreeing with the elders who advise Rehoboam.
notes.12:15: The noun sibbah ("turn of events"), derived from the root savav ("turn around"), occurs only here in the Hebrew Bible and denotes a divinely directed turning of affairs.
notes.12:24: The narrative from "At that time Abijah the son of Jeroboam fell ill" to the end of the verse is Masoretic 14:1-6, carried here following the Saints (Greek) verse arrangement; Masoretic 14:7-20 follow as additional verses. In Jeroboam's instructions to his wife, Ketiv preserves the archaic feminine pronoun atti while Qere reads standard att ("you").
notes.12:33: Ketiv reads mlbd ("apart/alone"), likely a scribal interchange of dalet and vav, while the translated Qere reads millibbo ("out of his own heart," i.e. of his own devising).
notes.13:2: The verb translated 'will be burned' is an impersonal third-person plural Qal imperfect (yisrefu, lit. 'they will burn'), a standard Hebrew construction expressing a passive sense.
notes.13:6: The phrase 'implore the favor of' renders the Piel idiom chillah et-peney (lit. 'soften' or 'appease the face of'), used of seeking divine mercy or goodwill.
notes.13:11: The Masoretic Text shifts from singular ('his son came and recounted to him') to plural ('they also recounted to their father') within the verse; this shift is retained rather than harmonized to the Septuagint.
notes.13:12: The Masoretic Text points the verb as a Qal (vayyir'u, 'saw' or 'had seen') rather than a Hiphil ('showed'), and is translated directly as pointed.
notes.13:33: 'Consecrate him' translates the priestly installation idiom yemalle et-yado (Piel of male', lit. 'fill his hand'). The final clause pairs a singular verb (vihi) with a plural predicate ('priests of the high places'), rendered as 'one of the priests of the high places.'
notes.14:24: Hebrew qadesh is a collective masculine singular noun (lit. 'consecrated one') denoting male shrine prostitutes. The phrase 'the abominations of the nations' reflects an unusual construction in which both nouns carry the definite article (hatto'evot haggoyim).
notes.14:25: Ketiv reads Shushaq (closer to Egyptian Shoshenq); Qere reads Shishak, which is followed in the translation.
notes.14:27: 'The guards' translates haratsim (Qal active participle of ruts, lit. 'the runners'), the standard title for the royal footguards and escorts.
notes.15:4: Hebrew nir, a by-form of ner ('lamp'), is used metaphorically for an enduring Davidic dynastic line (cf. 1 Kgs 11:36), though some scholars compare Akkadian niru ('yoke, dominion').
notes.15:13: The rare noun miphletset (from a root meaning 'to shudder') denotes an abominable or repulsive image made for Asherah; gebirah ('queen mother', lit. 'great lady') was an official royal title in Judah.
notes.15:15: Following the Qere (construct plural, 'and the dedicated things of', linked to 'the house of the LORD'); the Ketiv reads 'and his dedicated thing(s)', making 'the house of the LORD' the destination ('into the house of the LORD', cf. 2 Chr 15:18).
notes.15:23: Hebrew chalah et-raglav literally reads 'he became sick as to his feet', using the particle et to mark the affected body part (accusative of specification).
notes.16:3: The Hiphil participle mabir followed by achare ('sweeping away after') is an idiom for total eradication; the oracle also shifts abruptly from third person ('Baasha and his house') to second person ('your house').
notes.16:11: Literally 'one who urinates against a wall', an earthy Hebrew idiom for every male; 'close kinsmen' translates go'alav, referring to near relatives with the duty of blood vengeance.
notes.16:26: Following the Qere singular ('in his sin'); the Ketiv reads plural ('in his sins'). The noun rendered 'empty idols' literally means 'vapors' or 'emptinesses', a derisive term for false gods.
notes.16:34: Following the Qere spelling 'Segub' (Ketiv 'Segib'). The preposition be- before both sons' names expresses price ('at the cost of'), fulfilling Joshua's curse on Jericho (Josh 6:26).
notes.17:1: The Masoretic vocalization reads "from the settlers of Gilead" (from toshav, resident alien/settler) rather than a place name Tishbe. In Hebrew oaths, the conditional particle im followed by ki im ("except") expresses an emphatic negation.
notes.17:14: Ketiv reads ttn (an unusual infinitive or imperfect form of natan, "give"), while the Qere followed here reads tet, the standard Qal infinitive construct ("giving").
notes.17:15: Ketiv reads "he and she," while the Qere followed here reverses the order to "she and he," agreeing with the preceding feminine singular verb ("ate").
notes.17:21: "Stretched himself out" translates the Hithpolel of madad ("measure"); "life" renders nefesh ("life/soul"), and "into him" literally reads "upon his inward parts."
notes.18:5: "Cut off" translates the Hiphil of karat ("cut off/destroy"), deliberately echoing the same verb used in verse 4 for Jezebel cutting off the LORD's prophets.
notes.18:21: "Limping" translates the Qal participle of pasach ("limp/hop"), echoed in the Piel in verse 26 for the ritual limping of Baal's prophets; "divided opinions" renders a rare plural noun (seippim) related to "branches" or "divided thoughts."
notes.18:26: Both "was given" and "had been made" translate Masoretic Qal active third-person masculine singular verbs (natan and asah), rendered here as impersonal passives.
notes.18:27: "Stepped aside" translates a hapax legomenon (sig, "turning aside/withdrawal"), widely understood as a sarcastic euphemism for relieving oneself.
notes.18:36: Ketiv reads "at Your words" (plural), while the Qere followed here reads "at Your word" (singular).
notes.19:2: The plural verbs ya'asun and yosifun treat elohim as plural ('the gods') in Jezebel's oath. The Masoretic Text omits 'to me' and uses the asseverative oath particle ki ('surely') rather than a negative conditional.
notes.19:3: The Masoretic Text points wayyar' as Qal of ra'ah ('he saw'); some Hebrew manuscripts and ancient versions reflect yare' ('he was afraid').
notes.19:4: Ketiv reads the feminine numeral 'ahat ('one'), while Qere reads masculine 'ehad ('one') to agree with the masculine noun rotem ('broom bush').
notes.19:12: Hebrew qol demamah daqqah literally means 'a sound of thin/fine stillness' or 'delicate silence,' contrasting sharply with the violent wind, earthquake, and fire.
notes.19:21: Hebrew bishshelam habbasar ('boiled them, the meat') places a proleptic plural object suffix on the Piel verb bishshel referring to the oxen, clarified in apposition by habbasar ('the meat').
notes.20:8: Ketiv reads hassefarim ('the letters') with the definite article, while Qere reads sefarim ('letters') without the article.
notes.20:10: Hebrew berekhta (Piel of barakh, literally 'you have blessed') is a reverential euphemism for 'cursed' (so also in 20:13) to avoid pairing 'curse' directly with 'God.' 'Sons of worthlessness' (bene-veliyya'al) is a Hebrew idiom for base, unscrupulous scoundrels.
notes.20:21: 'Every male' renders the coarse Hebrew idiom mashtin beqir (literally 'one who urinates against a wall'). 'Both confined and free' renders the merism 'atsur ve'azuv (literally 'restrained and released/abandoned'), encompassing everyone without exception.
notes.20:23: The Masoretic Text reads behel ('by the rampart/outer wall'), distinct from beheleq ('in the plot/territory') in 2 Kings 9:10, 36.
notes.20:27: Hebrew wayhallekh 'at (Piel of halakh with 'at, literally 'walked about softly/gently') denotes a slow, subdued manner expressing humility and mourning.
notes.21:11: Hebrew reads literally "one who girds on" (Qal participle of חגר) and "one who unfastens" (Piel participle of פתח), with armor or battle gear implied.
notes.21:23: Hebrew אֱלֹהִים ("God/gods") is grammatically plural in form and here lacks a singular verb or pronoun, so the Aramean servants' remark can also be rendered "Their gods are gods of the mountains." Verse 28, however, explicitly reports their claim in the singular with "the LORD" and "He" (הוּא).
notes.21:33: The rare verb וַיַּחְלְטוּ (from חלט, occurring only here in Biblical Hebrew, meaning "confirm/decide/seize upon") followed by הֲמִמֶּנּוּ ("whether from him") follows the Masoretic vocalization and word division. Many commentators redivide the consonants as וַיַּחְלְטוּהָ מִמֶּנּוּ ("they snatched it [the word] from him").
notes.21:34: Hebrew חֻצוֹת ("streets") here refers to designated commercial quarters or trading bazaars. The Hebrew text marks no explicit speaker change before "And as for me," where Ahab replies to Ben-hadad's terms.
notes.21:41: Ketiv (written) reads מעל ("from over/off"); Qere (read) reads מֵעֲלֵי, the poetic or expanded form of the same preposition with identical meaning. The rare noun אֲפֵר (occurring only here and in v. 38) denotes a headband or bandage.
notes.22:6: The Hebrew text here reads Adonai ('the Lord') rather than the divine name ('the LORD'), contrasting with verses 12 and 15. The Hebrew also omits an explicit direct object for 'give' here and in verses 12 and 15, leaving the oracle's wording open-ended.
notes.22:13: Ketiv/Qere variant: the written ketiv is plural ('your words'), while the read qere translated here is singular ('your word'), agreeing with the singular verb 'let ... be' and the following singular 'word of one of them'.
notes.22:21: Hebrew uses the definite article ('the spirit'), likely pointing to a specific spirit in the heavenly vision or the spirit of prophecy rather than an indefinite 'a spirit'.
notes.22:30: Hebrew uses two infinitives absolute (Hithpael 'disguising' and Qal 'entering') with first-person force ('I will disguise myself and enter'), immediately contrasted with the emphatic second-person imperative 'while you put on your robes'.
notes.22:38: Hebrew literally has a concise circumstantial clause 'while the prostitutes bathed' (waw + subject + Qal perfect) without stating a location or object, following the rinsing of the chariot at the pool of Samaria.
